question: Who is the Title IX coordinator at Ramapo, and which office are they in?
good_reply: Kat McGee, J.D., Director of Title IX and Institutional Compliance (the Title IX Coordinator): Office D 104, (201) 684-7220, kmcgee@ramapo.edu.
must_not: Leaving out the office when asked. Invented people, numbers, rooms or dates.

body.answer:
Title IX: Kat McGee, J.D. Director of Title IX and Institutional Compliance: kmcgee@ramapo.edu To file a complaint at the College about an incident of discrimination and/or sexual misconduct: titleix@ramapo.edu [1] Title IX is in D-104. [1]

Title IX's page "Who is the College’s Director of Title IX/Title IX Coordinator?" says: "Kat McGee, J.D. Director of Title IX and Institutional Compliance Office: D 104 (201) 684-7220 kmcgee@ramapo.edu (mailto:kmcgee@ramapo.edu)" [2]

Title IX's page "What does the Director of Title IX/Title IX Coordinator do?" says: "The Director of Title IX is responsible for ensuring effective and timely responses to complaints of sexual violence, misconduct, discrimination or harassment by implementing Title IX related policies, coordinating appropriate training and resources, and identifying ways to prevent future discrimination. This includes management of grievances, investigations, and the disposition of complaints of sexual harassment, violence, rape, and discrimination under the Sexual Misconduct Policy ([https://www.ramapo.edu/titleix/sexual-misconduct-policy/](https://www.ramapo.edu/titleix/sexual-misconduct-policy/))." (more on its page) [2]

Title IX's page "Contact Information for Reporting" says: "Kat McGee, Director of Title IX and Institutional Compliance (available during regular business hours) Phone: (201) 684-7220 Office Location: D-104 kmcgee@ramapo.edu (mailto:kmcgee@ramapo.edu) The Public Safety Department (available 24 hours a day, 7 days a week) Phone: (201) 684-6666 Office Location: C-102 Handout: Title IX Reporting Requirements ([https://www.ramapo.edu/titleix/wp-content/uploads/sites/300/2026/10/Title-IX-Reporting-Requirements-FY27.pdf](https://www.ramapo.edu/titleix/wp-content/uploads/sites/300/2026/10/Title-IX-Reporting-Requirements-FY27.pdf))" [3]

Office of the General Counsel & Institutional Compliance's page "Contact" says: "Nicole Morgan-Agard, Esq. Vice President and General Counsel E-mail: nmagard@ramapo.edu (mailto:nmagard@ramapo.edu) Phone: (201) 684-7503 Paul Szypiotko, Esq., LSW Assistant General Counsel E-mail: pszypiot@ramapo.edu Phone: (201) 684-7610 Stacy Storms Paralegal Email: sstorms@ramapo.edu (mailto:sstorms@ramapo.edu) Phone: (201) 684-7865 Kat McGee, J.D. Director of Title IX and Institutional Compliance Email: kmcgee@ramapo.edu (mailto:kmcgee@ramapo.edu) Phone: (201) 684-7220 Office: D-104A Jineane Miller Lajam Administrative Assistant E-mail: jmillerl@rampo.edu (mailto:jmillerl@rampo.edu) Phone: (201) 684-6693 Gina Mayer-Costa Director of Environmental Health & Safety E-mail: gmayerco@ramapo.edu (mailto:gmayerco@ramapo.edu) Phone: (201) 684-7531 Evan Kutzin Fire Marshal E-mail:ekutzin@ramapo.edu (mailto:ekutzin@ramapo.edu) Phone: (201) 684-6252 Samuel Antoshak Fire and Safety Specialist E-mail: santosha@ramapo.edu (mailto:santosha@ramapo.edu) Phone: (201)…" (more on its page) [4]

Yes. The Technology Animation Studies Club welcomes Pokémon fans; its page says you can play cards, DS, or Nintendo games, but doesn’t list meeting times. Email: tasc@ramapo.edu. [7] The Center for Student Involvement is the office listed for this club. [7]

question: how do i start my own club
good_reply: Through the Student Government Association: the SGA Vice President explains how to start a club, and SGA's Club Process & Allocations Committee reviews the proposed constitution and the Archway application. Contact sga@ramapo.edu.
must_not: Only how to join an existing club. Invented people, numbers, rooms or dates.

body.answer:

2. Center for Student Involvement: If you browse through this list and find your interests are not represented, inquire about starting a new club or organization [4].
3. Center for Student Involvement: Once the College recognizes an organization, it is eligible to receive financial support from the Student Activities Allocations Committee [4].

question: tell me about the MPP
good_reply: The Public Policy MPP (Master of Public Policy) in the School of Social Sciences and Social Work, from its catalog description. The Public Policy 4+1 may be added.
must_not: Saying there is no such program; describing another program.

body.answer:
The Public Policy MPP is the Master of Public Policy in the School of Social Sciences and Social Work. It focuses on how government laws and policies shape lives, and trains students in research methods and skills for work with or for public institutions. Other published levels: Public Policy 4+1 and Public Policy Minor. [1]

Requirements: all of PUBL 600 The Politics of Policymaking; 601 Federal Public Policy & Governance; 602 State & Local Public Policy; 616 Econometrics and Analysis; 618 Public Management; 621 Political Economy; and 705 Public Policy Internship. Select 3 electives from: ACCT 502 Government and Not-for-Profit Accounting; ACCT 625 International Accounting; BADM 501 Data Analytics; BADM 503 Business Law, Ethics & Regulatory Pronouncements; DATA 601 Introduction to Data Science; DATA 670 Data Visualization; MATH 570 Applied Statistics; MATH 685 Introduction to Experimental Design; MBAD 610 Becoming a 21st Century Leader; MBAD 625 Crisis & Change Management; NURS 660 Leadership and Innovation in Healthcare; NURS 670 Healthcare Economics and Finance; NURS 808 Health Policy Leadership; MSWK 505 Social Welfare Programs and Policies I; MSWK 507 Cultural Diversity, Racism, Oppression and Privilege; MSWK 604 Advanced Social Policy; MSWK 610 Public Health in West Africa; MSWK 670 Social Welfare Policies in Health and Mental Health. [1]

Graduate Admissions requires one professional or academic recommendation: enter references’ names and contact information in “Recommendations” in the online application; Ramapo sends the request, and references upload recommendations to the application portal. The recommendation is waived for current Ramapo students graduating in 2027 and recent Ramapo graduates from 2025 and 2026. Also submit a 400-word personal statement about your interest, intellectual development, and goals, and a resume. [6]

**Graduate Admissions**: Phone: (201) 684-7270. Email: graduate@ramapo.edu. Location: McBride House. [12]

Sources: [1](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/programs/SO-MPP-PBPL) [6](https://www.ramapo.edu/graduate/requirements/) [12](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/)

question: what's the RN to BSN
good_reply: The Nursing RN to BSN track, for registered nurses with an associate's degree or diploma who return for the BSN; one of three BSN tracks (generic, accelerated, RN to BSN); accredited by ACEN.
must_not: Invented people, numbers, rooms or dates.

body.answer:
The Nursing RN to BSN is a Bachelor of Science in Nursing track for registered nurses prepared at the Associate’s degree or Diploma level who are returning to pursue a BSN. Students transfer credits from their initial nursing program and complete Ramapo’s general education and nursing requirements. Ramapo’s Nursing programs are accredited by the Accreditation Commission for Education in Nursing (ACEN). Diploma-program graduates are granted 30 credits for their diploma nursing courses upon satisfactory completion of their first two BSN nursing courses. [1]

Requirements:
- Required Math Course—select 1: MATH 108 Elementary Probability and Statistics; PSYC 242 Statistics; or SOCI 308 Data Analysis in Sociology.
- RN to BSN Professional Core—required courses all of: NURS 312 Nursing Informatics; NURS 316 Pathophysiology; NURS 325 Nursing Research and Evidence Based Practice; NURS 330 Health Assessment Across the Lifespan; NURS 425 Community Centered Nursing; NURS 445 Leadership in a Global World; and NURS 460 Clinical Management.
- Elective—select 1. Students should consult their Nursing advisor for elective course options. [1]

Other published levels: Nursing Accelerated BSN, Nursing Generic BSN, and Nursing MSN. [1]

Sources: [1](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/programs/SN-BSN-NURS)

question: how many classes is the public health minor and which ones count
good_reply: Five courses: BIOL 204 Epidemiology, plus one each from statistics/research methods, health policy and management, social and behavioral science, and global or population health, with examples from each list.
must_not: Leaving out a course group. Invented people, numbers, rooms or dates.

body.answer:
The Public Health Minor consists of five courses (20 credits). [1] You must take BIOL 204 EPIDEMIOLOGY, plus one course from each of these groups: [1]

- Statistics or Research Methods: BADM 225 MANAGEMENT STATISTICS; ENSC 345 RESEARCH DESIGN & STATISTICS; MATH 370 APPLIED STATISTICS; NURS 325 NURSING RESEARCH AND EVIDENCE BASED PRACTICE; PSYC 242 STATISTICS; PSYC 303 RESEARCH METHODS IN PSYCHOLOGY; SOCI 307 SOCIAL RESEARCH WITH COMPUTERS; or SWRK 307 SOCIAL WORK RESEARCH METHODS. [1]
- Health Policy and Management: COMM 383 THEORY AND PRACTICE OF HEALTH COMMUNICATION; ECON 332 HEALTH ECONOMICS: AN INTERNATIONAL PERSPECTIVE; ENST 317 ENVIRONMENTAL POLICY AND REGULATION; MGMT 330 HEALTHCARE ADMINISTRATION; NURS 445 LEADERSHIP IN A GLOBAL WORLD; or PUBL 201 PRINCIPLES OF PUBLIC POLICY. [1]
- Social and Behavioral Science: SCIN 310 AIDS: BIOLOGICAL, MEDICAL, SOCIAL PERSPECTIVES; SOCI 230 SOCIOLOGY OF HEALTH & MEDICINE; SWRK 230 AIDS: SOCIAL PERSPECTIVES; SWRK 328 COMMUNITY MENTAL HEALTH; PHLT 305 HEALTH AND WELLNESS; or PHLT 390 TOPICS. [1]
- Global or Population Health: ANTH 307 MEDICAL ANTHROPOLOGY; NURS 220 COMMUNITY HEALTH AND TRADITIONAL CHINESE MEDICINE; NURS 365 PUBLIC HEALTH IN WEST AFRICA; NURS 425 COMMUNITY CENTERED NURSING; PHLT 290 TOPICS; SOCI 309 FOOD AND POPULATION; or SPAN 311 SPANISH FOR HEALTH CARE AND HUMAN SERVICES PROFESSIONALS. [1]

BIOL 204 is 4 credits; its prerequisite is BIOL 111 FUNDAMENTALS OF BIOLOGY I LECTURE (complete all). [3] PHLT 305, PHLT 390 and PHLT 290 are each 4 credits and have no published prerequisites. [6][5][4] PHLT 300 IS-PUBLIC HEALTH and ENST 355 ENVIRONMENTAL HEALTH are not listed in the minor requirements. [1]

Sources: [1](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/programs/SN-MN-PHLT) [3](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/courses/BIOL204) [4](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/courses/PHLT290) [5](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/courses/PHLT390) [6](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/courses/PHLT305)

question: what happens if i take an incomplete and don't finish the work in time? can i get more time
good_reply: An I needs the instructor's approval and at least two-thirds of the course done. Work not finished by the date on the academic calendar turns the I into an F. In extraordinary circumstances a student can request an extension, up to the end of the following semester, on the Registrar's form with the student's signature and the faculty member's approval, due by the last day to resolve incompletes (Feb 12, 2027 for fall incompletes).
must_not: Leaving out that it becomes an F, or that an extension exists. Invented people, numbers, rooms or dates.

body.answer:
The Fall 2026 academic calendar lists [21]:
- Friday, October 16, 2026: Session I Courses - Last Day to Request an Incomplete ("I" Grade) (already passed)
- Tuesday, December 15, 2026: Full and Session II Courses - Last Day to Request an Incomplete ("I" Grade)

Yes, in extraordinary circumstances you may request an incomplete extension. [6] Registrar: If the work is completed by the completion date on the Incomplete Form or the academic calendar, whichever is earlier, the assigned grade replaces the I; if it is not satisfactorily completed by then, the grade changes to F. [4] Review the Academic Calendar ([https://www.ramapo.edu/academic-calendars/](https://www.ramapo.edu/academic-calendars/)) for incomplete deadlines, and the student and instructor must complete the Incomplete Form. [4] Submit the form to the Office of the Registrar at reg@ramapo.edu. [4] An extension may last only until the end of the semester following the semester the incomplete grade was given. [6] Obtain the incomplete extension form from the Office of the Registrar; it requires the student’s signature and faculty approval. [6] Submit the extension to the Office of the Registrar by the last day to resolve an incomplete grade posted on the Academic Calendar. [6]

**Registrar**: Phone: (201) 684-7695. Email: reg@ramapo.edu. Office: D-224. [22]

question: whats the max credits i can take in a semester and can i go over it
good_reply: 18 credits a semester. More needs a credit overload request through the Registrar (form), at extra cost; the GPA rule is 3.0 (the catalog says a student under 3.0 needs the advisor's approval first), and over 20 credits needs the school dean's approval.
must_not: Leaving out how to go over the limit. Invented people, numbers, rooms or dates.

body.answer:
The typical maximum is 18 credits per semester, and you can request to go over it. [9]
Office of the Provost: For Fall and Spring, a matriculated student requesting more than 18 credits must ask the Office of the Registrar to raise the limit, at additional cost. [2] If your cumulative GPA is under 3.0, you need approval from your academic advisor before making that request. [2] More than 20 credits also requires approval from your school Dean. [2]
Center for Student Success (Academic Advising): To be granted an overload, you must have above a 3.0 GPA or be a graduating senior. [9]
Registrar: The overload request form is for undergraduates seeking more than 18 credits or graduate students seeking more than their program maximum. [12] An overload is granted only if you have a 3.0 GPA or above. [12]

- **Center for Student Success (Academic Advising)**: Phone: (201) 684-7441. Email: success@ramapo.edu. Office: D-207. [25]
- **Office of the Provost**: Phone: (201) 684-7330. Email: provost@ramapo.edu. Location: first floor of the Birch Mansion. [25]

Sources: [2](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/pages/R532kjMfIcfnIkM0srb3#credit-load) [9](https://www.ramapo.edu/studentsuccess/policies/) [12](https://www.ramapo.edu/registrar/credit-overload-request-form/) [25](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/)

pageFacts.question: whats the max credits i can take in a semester and can i go over it

facts.says: Fall and Spring A matriculated student who wishes to register for more than 18 credits per semester (at additional cost) must request that the Office of the Registrar raise their credit limit.
If the student has under a 3.0 cumulative GPA, that student must obtain approval to raise the credit limit from their academic advisor prior to making the request to the Office of the Registrar.
If the student is attempting to register for more than 20 credits, they must obtain approval from their school Dean.
A student is typically permitted to take up to 18 credits per semester.
However, a student can request to take more than the allotted 18 credits by applying for a credit overload.
The student must have above a 3.0 GPA or be a graduating senior to be granted the credit overload.
The credit overload request form can be found here (https://www.ramapo.edu/registrar/credit-overload-request-form/).
The credit overload request form is used when an undergraduate student wishes to take more than 18 credits or a graduate student that wishes to take more than the maximum for their program.
A credit overload is ONLY granted if the student has a 3.0 GPA or above.
Credit overloads will incur additional charges. Δ

good_reply: Within 20 calendar days after grades post, appeal in writing (email or certified letter) to the instructor with documentation; they have 15 days to decide. body.answer:
That's stressful, but one bad grade doesn't decide everything. Talking with your professor and an advisor soon can really help.

The first deadline is no later than twenty calendar days after the posting of grades. [3]

Office of the Provost:

3. pageFacts.question: i think my final grade is wrong, how do i appeal it and is there a deadline

facts.says: Circumstances for which students may appeal gradesGrade appeals will be considered only if a student can provide documentation supporting their case.

Circumstances that might justify a grade appeal include (but are not limited to): computational error; factual information not in evidence at the time the grade was posted (for example, an assignment that the student can document was submitted but was not graded by the course instructor and therefore not factored into the final grade); or an alleged violation of College Policy.

If circumstances such as those described above can be documented, the student may appeal a grade by taking the following steps: No later than twenty calendar days after the posting of grades, a student must bring their appeal to the attention of the course instructor in writing by email or certified letter.
Supporting documentation must be provided.
Both parties should make good faith efforts to share viewpoints and mediate differences of opinion.
Students and instructors have up to 15 calendar days to reach a determination of grade.

If a student and the course instructor cannot reach an agreement and a student wishes to further pursue a grade appeal, the student must present a written appeal (by email or certified letter), including pertinent course materials or course work, to the Dean of the academic unit which sponsored the course in question within twenty calendar days of the final determination conference between the student and the course instructor.

The Dean will confer with the student and the course instructor, jointly or independently as they see fit, review pertinent documents and course materials, and confer with other faculty or administrative staff members as appropriate.
If the Dean determines that a grade change is not warranted, the course instructor and student will be so informed in writing by email.
The Deans have 15 calendar days to make this determination.

question: if i drop a class and go part time will i lose my financial aid
good_reply: Aid is adjusted below full time (12 credits): federal aid needs at least 6 credits; going from 12 to 6 reduces a Pell Grant but federal loans can be kept; state aid may be canceled; Ramapo grants and scholarships (merit scholarships need 12 credits) may be reduced or taken away. Talk to Financial Aid before dropping.
must_not: Leading with "I can't see your records" instead of the rules (a short note at the end is fine). Invented people, numbers, rooms or dates.

body.answer:
It depends. Financial Aid says that if you drop below full-time status, your aid will be adjusted; federal aid requires 6 credits in a semester, and federal aid should not be affected if you remain enrolled for 6 or more credits. [1][2] If you go from full time status 12 credits to part time status 6 credits, your federal pell will be reduced but you can keep your federal loans. [1] NJ State aid (ie TAG, EOF, etc) requires full-time enrollment when the aid is fully disbursed to your account. [2] If you drop below full-time status, which is less than 12 credits, your Academic Scholarship or Ramapo grant may be taken away or reduced for the semester. [3] Financial Aid asks you to contact the Office of Financial Aid before making a change that drops you below full-time status. [3]

**Financial Aid**: Phone: (201) 684-7549. Email: finaid@ramapo.edu. Office: E-210. [11]

Sources: [1](https://www.ramapo.edu/finaid/faqs/) [2](https://www.ramapo.edu/finaid/faqs/) [3](https://www.ramapo.edu/finaid/academic-merit-scholarships-terms-conditions/) [11](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/)

Visit Valley Medical Group Health Services (https://www.valleyhealth.com/ramapo-college-health-services) for immunization information and instructions on how to upload any documentation regarding immunization.

question: i have a medical condition, how can i request a housing accommodation
good_reply: Step 1: register with OSS (Application for Affiliation plus documentation from a licensed provider). Step 2: the Housing Accommodation Student Request Form and Provider Documentation Form. Step 3: meet Residence Life's deadlines. A committee (OSS, Residence Life, Health, Counseling) decides within 21 business days of complete documentation. OSS: 201-684-7514, oss@ramapo.edu, C-205.
must_not: Leaving out a step. Invented people, numbers, rooms or dates.

body.answer:
You can ask for support with that.

1. **Office of Specialized Services (OSS):** First register for affiliation with OSS to request a housing accommodation based on a disability. [3]
2. **Office of Specialized Services (OSS):** Submit comprehensive disability documentation from a licensed physician, psychiatrist, psychologist, social worker, or certified learning disabilities specialist. [3]
3. **Office of Specialized Services (OSS):** See “How To Request OSS Services” ([https://www.ramapo.edu/oss/how-to-request-oss-services/](https://www.ramapo.edu/oss/how-to-request-oss-services/)) for more information. [3]
4. **Office of Specialized Services (OSS):** If you are requesting only a strobe alarm, roll-in shower, wheelchair/mobility accessible residence hall, or 1st floor, you do not need to complete the Housing Accommodation Student or Provider Request Forms; complete a request for disability support form instead. [3]
5. **Housing & Residence Life:** Once you are affiliated, OSS informs the Office of Residence Life of residents who need specific housing accommodations based on medical documentation provided to OSS. [1]

- **Office of Specialized Services**: Phone: (201) 684-7514. Email: oss@ramapo.edu. Location: C-Wing, Room 205. [11]
- **Housing & Residence Life**: Phone: (201) 684-7461. Email: reslife@ramapo.edu. [11]

Sources: [1](https://www.ramapo.edu/reslife/apply/) [3](https://www.ramapo.edu/oss/housing-accommodations/) [11](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/)

citations.title: #1 - Register with the Office of Specialized Services

pageFacts.question: i have a medical condition, how can i request a housing accommodation

facts.says: Any resident, who is requesting specific housing accommodations, due to a medically related condition, will need to register with the Office of Specialized Services (OSS).
Once affiliated, OSS will inform the Office of Residence Life of any residents who require specific housing accommodations based on medical documentation provided to their office.
Please submit requests for housing accommodations no later than published deadlines.
Phone 201-684-7514 Email: oss@ramapo.edu www.ramapo.edu/oss
All students requesting a housing accommodation based on a disability must first register for affiliation with the Office of Specialized Services (OSS).
Check out our webpage “How To Request OSS Services” (https://www.ramapo.edu/oss/how-to-request-oss-services/) for more information.

Comprehensive documentation of a disability from a licensed physician, psychiatrist, psychologist, social worker, or certified learning disabilities specialist must be submitted in order to establish eligibility and to determine which accommodations and/or adjustments are appropriate for each student.

Note: Students requesting only a strobe alarm, roll-in shower, wheelchair/mobility accessible residence hall, or 1st floor do not need to complete the Housing Accommodation Student or Provider Request Forms, as below.
Students only need to complete a request for disability support form.
Students can expect a decision about their request within twenty one (21) business days of OSS receiving all requested documentation.

question: i broke my wrist and cant write for a few weeks. can OSS help me with notes and exams
good_reply: Yes, OSS serves students with temporary disabilities such as a broken limb: submit the Application for Disability Support and current documentation, then an intake meeting with the OSS Director or Assistant Director authorizes accommodations. OSS: 201-684-7514, oss@ramapo.edu, C-205.
must_not: Saying OSS only helps permanent disabilities. Invented people, numbers, rooms or dates.

body.answer:
I'm sorry you're dealing with that, and I hope you feel better soon.

Yes. The Office of Specialized Services supports students with temporary disabilities; appropriate services are discussed and authorized based on current functional limitations [13]. Potential accommodations include notetakers, scribes, extended testing time, or alternative testing arrangements [14].
1. Schedule a meeting on Connect with your OSS Counselor and request a notetaker to review your accommodations for the semester [4].
2. After meeting with your OSS Counselor and/or requesting accommodations, make exam reservations through OSSOline for exams in your classes [5].

**Office of Specialized Services**: Phone: (201) 684-7514. Email: oss@ramapo.edu. Location: C-Wing, Room 205. [23]

This office can help:
**Health Services**: Phone: (201) 684-7536. Location: Near the campus South Gate entrance at the corner of Route 202 and Hornbeam Road. [24]

Sources: [4](https://www.ramapo.edu/oss/notetaking/) [5](https://www.ramapo.edu/oss/ossonline-info-tutorials/) [13](https://www.ramapo.edu/oss/oss-services-accommodations/) [14](https://www.ramapo.edu/oss/disabilities-and-teaching-strategies-accommodations/) [23](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/) [24](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/)

Alternative Testing/Exam Reservations After you have met with your OSS Counselor and/or requested your accommodations, you can begin using OSSOline to make alternative testing exam reservations that you have in each class.
Log into OSSOnline to review your courses and select your accommodations for the semester.
After you select the accommodations you choose in OSSOnline, your OSS Counselor is notified to review and approve your accommodations.
OSS students will submit an exam reservation through OSSOnline no later than 7 days prior to the scheduled on campus exam and 14 days prior to the on campus final exam.
The Office of Specialized Services provides information and support services to Ramapo College students with permanent and temporary disabilities.
During this appointment, appropriate support services will be discussed and authorized, based on the current functional limitations that may result from the disability.

After students meet with their OSS Counselor, they can review their accommodation plan and make accommodation and exam requests online by logging into OSSOnline (http://accessiblelearning.com/ramapo).
A mobility impairment may impact, to varying degrees, a student’s ability to manipulate objects, turn pages, write with a pen or pencil, type at a keyboard, and/or retrieve research materials.

Potential Accommodations / Teaching Strategies: Accessible locations for classrooms, labs, and field trips Wide aisles and uncluttered work areas Adjustable height and tilt tables; equipment located within reach Notetakers, scribes, and lab assistants Extended testing time or alternative testing arrangements Computers with speech input and alternative keyboards Course materials available in electronic format For courses that include field trips or internships, OSS can help identify and coordinate accommodations.

question: can i have an emotional support animal in my dorm, and how does approval work
good_reply: Call OSS at 201-684-7514 and meet with the OSS Director; documentation from a health care or mental health professional is needed; the animal may come only after OSS approval (Residence Life pets rule); it may be limited to defined areas, generally not academic or recreational buildings.
must_not: Invented people, numbers, rooms or dates.

body.answer:
It depends: you may have an emotional support animal on campus if you have registered with the Office of Specialized Services (OSS), provided disability documentation demonstrating the benefits of the animal, and received an accommodation permitting the animal on campus [2]. The Office of Specialized Services says you must affiliate with OSS by providing documentation verifying your disability and need for the requested accommodation; OSS staff and, in most cases, the Housing Accommodation Request Committee review the request [5]. OSS and/or the committee may deny requests that are unreasonable or insufficiently documented [4].

question: i got a parking ticket. how do i pay or appeal it and how long do i have
good_reply: Appeal online within 20 days of the citation (appeal form; reviewed by the Parking Appeals Board). A citation not paid or appealed within 20 days gets a $5 late fee (another $5 after 28 days), and the right to appeal is lost after 20 days. Payment as the page says.
must_not: Leaving out the 20-day limit. Invented people, numbers, rooms or dates.

body.answer:
Public Safety: You have twenty (20) days from the citation’s issuance to submit an online appeal; after that, you forfeit the right to appeal. [1][1] Citations not paid or appealed within 20 days are subject to a $5 late fee, and a second $5 late fee may be assessed after 28 days. [3][3]

1. Pay online at [https://rcnjpublicsafety.omnigo.one/CESIReportExec/OCP/Main.aspx](https://rcnjpublicsafety.omnigo.one/CESIReportExec/OCP/Main.aspx): enter Citation # and Fine Amount, search, select your citation, follow the required fields, then select a payment method. Once processed, an email will confirm it is paid. [4]
2. Appeal online at [https://cm.maxient.com/reportingform.php?RamapoCollege&layout_id=3](https://cm.maxient.com/reportingform.php?RamapoCollege&layout_id=3). Identify the specific ground(s) for your appeal and briefly explain your justification. [1][2]

- **Public Safety (Non-Emergency)**: Phone: (201) 684-7432. Email: publicsafety@ramapo.edu. Office: C-102. [23]
- **Public Safety (Emergency)**: Phone: (201) 684-6666. Email: publicsafety@ramapo.edu. Office: C-102. [23]

Sources: [1](https://www.ramapo.edu/publicsafety/vehicle-citation-information/) [2](https://www.ramapo.edu/publicsafety/parking-regulations/) [3](https://www.ramapo.edu/publicsafety/parking-regulations/) [4](https://www.ramapo.edu/publicsafety/vehicle-citation-information/) [23](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/)

facts.says: How to Appeal Your Parking Citation Click Here to Go to the Appeal Portal (https://cm.maxient.com/reportingform.php?RamapoCollege&layout_id=3) Appeals are input online via the form An online appeal by the owner/driver must be made within twenty (20) days of the issuance of a citation.
Failure to file the appeal within twenty (20) days constitutes forfeiture of the right to appeal.

Appeals will not be considered for: Ignorance of the regulation Stated inability to find a legal parking space Operation of the vehicle by another person Stated failure of parking enforcement staff to ticket previously for similar offenses Inability to pay the fine Disagreement with Motor Vehicle Rules and Regulations Citations issued by the Mahwah Police Department Appellants must identify upon which specific ground(s) they are appealing and briefly describe their justification.
IMPORTANT CONSIDERATIONS: Citations not paid or appealed within 20 days are subject to a $5 late fee.
The ability to appeal is forfeit if the appeal is not submitted within 20 days.
A second $5 late fee may be assessed after 28 days.

How to Pay for Your Parking Citation Online Click Here to Go to the Payment Portal (https://rcnjpublicsafety.omnigo.one/CESIReportExec/OCP/Main.aspx) Citations are paid online using the portal Enter Citation # and Fine Amount Search for Citation Select your Citation and follow the field required.
Select Payment Method Once processed your citation will be emailed to you to say that it is paid

question: how do i pay my student account bill online
good_reply: Log in to RCNJ Experience (Web Self-Service), open the Student Account Info card, then Bill & Payment Suite and Make Payment; pay by electronic check (checking/savings) or credit/debit card via PayPath. Bills are eBills only; a monthly payment plan exists. Student Accounts: studentaccts@ramapo.edu, (201) 684-7495.
must_not: Anything about the Accounting program.

body.answer:
Student Accounts:
1. Log into RCNJ Experience (Web Self-Service) ([https://experience.elluciancloud.com/rconj/](https://experience.elluciancloud.com/rconj/)), locate the Student Account Info card, click Bill & Payment Suite, then click the Make Payment tab. [6]
2. Select the term, click Continue, choose Credit Card via PayPath from the Payment Method drop-down, then click Select. Verify or modify the payment amount and click Continue to PayPath. [6]
3. Read the non-refundable PayPath service fee disclaimer and click Continue. Review the payment amount information and click Continue; enter your Credit/Debit Card Billing Information and click Continue. [6]
4. Review your entries. Click Change Information if anything is incorrect, or Cancel if you do not want the transaction processed. Click Submit to submit the payment; submitting accepts the non-refundable service fee. Print the Payment Confirmation Page for your records. The College reserves the right to change costs, dates and procedures at its discretion. [6]

**Student Accounts**: Phone: (201) 684-7495. Email: studentaccts@ramapo.edu. Location: D-Wing, First Floor. [11]

Sources: [6](https://www.ramapo.edu/student-accounts/methods/) [11](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/)

question: Who is the Title IX coordinator at Ramapo, and which office are they in?
good_reply: Kat McGee, J.D., Director of Title IX and Institutional Compliance (the Title IX Coordinator): Office D 104, (201) 684-7220, kmcgee@ramapo.edu.
must_not: Leaving out the office when asked. Invented people, numbers, rooms or dates.

body.answer:
Title IX phone: (201) 684-7220. [1] Title IX is in D-104. [1] Title IX: Kat McGee, J.D. Director of Title IX and Institutional Compliance: kmcgee@ramapo.edu To file a complaint at the College about an incident of discrimination and/or sexual misconduct: titleix@ramapo.edu [1]

Title IX's page "Who is the College’s Director of Title IX/Title IX Coordinator?" says: "Kat McGee, J.D. Director of Title IX and Institutional Compliance Office: D 104 (201) 684-7220 kmcgee@ramapo.edu (mailto:kmcgee@ramapo.edu)" [2]

Title IX's page "What does the Director of Title IX/Title IX Coordinator do?" says: "The Director of Title IX is responsible for ensuring effective and timely responses to complaints of sexual violence, misconduct, discrimination or harassment by implementing Title IX related policies, coordinating appropriate training and resources, and identifying ways to prevent future discrimination. value.text: Kat McGee, J.D. Director of Title IX and Institutional Compliance Office: D 104 (201) 684-7220 kmcgee@ramapo.edu (mailto:kmcgee@ramapo.edu)

value.heading: What does the Director of Title IX/Title IX Coordinator do?
value.text: The Director of Title IX is responsible for ensuring effective and timely responses to complaints of sexual violence, misconduct, discrimination or harassment by implementing Title IX related policies, coordinating appropriate training and resources, and identifying ways to prevent future discrimination. This includes management of grievances, investigations, and the disposition of complaints of sexual harassment, violence, rape, and discrimination under the Sexual Misconduct Policy (https://www.ramapo.edu/titleix/sexual-misconduct-policy/). The Director of Title IX is responsible for monitoring the overall implementation of Title IX for the College and coordinating compliance efforts. The Director helps to ensure that all students, staff, administrators, and faculty are trained and educated about Title IX. The Director of Title IX reports to the Office of the General Counsel & Institutional Compliance.

(see https://www.ramapo.edu/eof-program/) [office-pages](https://www.ramapo.edu/eof-program/)

Please ensure all required documents are submitted by June 5. EOF Advisors are available for both in-person and virtual meetings. good_reply: You Can Narcan! on Mon Nov 16 at 6 PM (College Park Apartments).
must_not: Saying nothing is listed. Invented people, numbers, rooms or dates.

body.answer:
The calendar lists 1 event in the next 14 days, Wednesday, November 4 to Wednesday, November 18 that matches what you asked (of 119 events then) [1]:

- 6 PM to 7 PM: You Can Narcan! (College Park Apartments) [2]

Yes. “You Can Narcan!” is Monday, November 16, 2026, 6 PM to 7 PM, at College Park Apartments. It’s free and includes a demonstration on using Naloxone; the first 20 people get free grab bags, and students can ask questions and try it afterward. [3]

question: tell me about the MPP
good_reply: The Public Policy MPP (Master of Public Policy) in the School of Social Sciences and Social Work, from its catalog description. The Public Policy 4+1 may be added.
must_not: Saying there is no such program; describing another program.

body.answer:
The Public Policy MPP is the Master of Public Policy in the School of Social Sciences and Social Work. It focuses on how laws and policies shape people’s lives, and trains students in research methodologies, quantitative and qualitative methods, and skills for working with or for public institutions. [1]

Requirements: all seven required courses—PUBL 600 THE POLITICS OF POLICYMAKING; PUBL 601 FEDERAL PUBLIC POLICY & GOVERNANCE; PUBL 602 STATE & LOCAL PUBLIC POLICY; PUBL 616 ECONOMETRICS AND ANALYSIS; PUBL 618 PUBLIC MANAGEMENT; PUBL 621 POLITICAL ECONOMY; and PUBL 705 PUBLIC POLICY INTERNSHIP. Select 3 at least 3 electives from the catalog’s list: ACCT 502 GOVERNMENT AND NOT-FOR-PROFIT ACCOUNTING; ACCT 625 INTERNATIONAL ACCOUNTING; BADM 501 DATA ANALYTICS; BADM 503 BUSINESS LAW, ETHICS & REGULATORY PRONOUNCEMENTS; DATA 601 INTRODUCTION TO DATA SCIENCE; DATA 670 DATA VISUALIZATION; MATH 570 APPLIED STATISTICS; MATH 685 INTRODUCTION TO EXPERIMENTAL DESIGN; MBAD 610 BECOMING A 21ST CENTURY LEADER; MBAD 625 CRISIS & CHANGE MANAGEMENT; NURS 660 LEADERSHIP AND INNOVATION IN HEALTHCARE; NURS 670 HEALTHCARE ECONOMICS AND FINANCE; NURS 808 HEALTH POLICY LEADERSHIP; MSWK 505 SOCIAL WELFARE PROGRAMS AND POLICIES I; MSWK 507 CULTURAL DIVERSITY, RACISM, OPPRESSION AND PRIVILEGE; MSWK 604 ADVANCED SOCIAL POLICY; MSWK 610 PUBLIC HEALTH IN WEST AFRICA; MSWK 670 SOCIAL WELFARE POLICIES IN HEALTH AND MENTAL HEALTH. [1]

Also published: Public Policy 4+1 and Public Policy Minor. [1]

The admissions page lists one letter of recommendation (professional or academic); enter references’ names and contact information in the online application’s ‘Recommendations’ section. Ramapo sends them an automated request, and they can upload directly to the application portal. The letter is waived for current Ramapo students graduating in 2027 and recent Ramapo graduates from 2025 and 2026. It also lists a 400-word personal statement describing your interest, fit with personal intellectual development, and what you expect to accomplish, plus a resume. [6]

For admissions questions, contact Graduate Admissions. [6]

**Graduate Admissions**: Phone: (201) 684-7270. Email: graduate@ramapo.edu. Location: McBride House. [15]

Sources: [1](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/programs/SO-MPP-PBPL) [6](https://www.ramapo.edu/graduate/requirements/) [15](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/)

question: what's the RN to BSN
good_reply: The Nursing RN to BSN track, for registered nurses with an associate's degree or diploma who return for the BSN; one of three BSN tracks (generic, accelerated, RN to BSN); accredited by ACEN.
must_not: Invented people, numbers, rooms or dates.

body.answer:
Nursing RN to BSN is a Bachelor of Science in Nursing track for registered nurses prepared at the Associate’s degree or Diploma level who are returning to pursue a BSN. Students transfer credits from their initial nursing program and complete Ramapo’s general education and nursing requirements. Ramapo’s nursing programs are accredited by the Accreditation Commission for Education in Nursing (ACEN). Diploma-program graduates are granted 30 credits for diploma nursing courses upon satisfactory completion of their first two BSN nursing courses. [1]

Requirements: Select 1 math course: MATH 108 ELEMENTARY PROBABILITY AND STATISTICS, PSYC 242 STATISTICS, or SOCI 308 DATA ANALYSIS IN SOCIOLOGY. Complete all required RN to BSN Professional Core courses: NURS 312 NURSING INFORMATICS; NURS 316 PATHOPHYSIOLOGY; NURS 325 NURSING RESEARCH AND EVIDENCE BASED PRACTICE; NURS 330 HEALTH ASSESSMENT ACROSS THE LIFESPAN; NURS 425 COMMUNITY CENTERED NURSING; NURS 445 LEADERSHIP IN A GLOBAL WORLD; and NURS 460 CLINICAL MANAGEMENT. Select 1 elective; students should consult their Nursing advisor for elective course options. [1]

Also published: Nursing Accelerated BSN, Nursing Generic BSN, and Nursing MSN. [1]

Sources: [1](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/programs/SN-BSN-NURS)

question: how many classes is the public health minor and which ones count
good_reply: Five courses: BIOL 204 Epidemiology, plus one each from statistics/research methods, health policy and management, social and behavioral science, and global or population health, with examples from each list.
must_not: Leaving out a course group. Invented people, numbers, rooms or dates.

body.answer:
The Public Health Minor consists of five courses (20 credits). [1]

Requirements: BIOL 204 EPIDEMIOLOGY (required); one Statistics or Research Methods course: BADM 225 MANAGEMENT STATISTICS, ENSC 345 RESEARCH DESIGN & STATISTICS, MATH 370 APPLIED STATISTICS, NURS 325 NURSING RESEARCH AND EVIDENCE BASED PRACTICE, PSYC 242 STATISTICS, PSYC 303 RESEARCH METHODS IN PSYCHOLOGY, SOCI 307 SOCIAL RESEARCH WITH COMPUTERS, or SWRK 307 SOCIAL WORK RESEARCH METHODS; one Health Policy and Management course: COMM 383 THEORY AND PRACTICE OF HEALTH COMMUNICATION, ECON 332 HEALTH ECONOMICS: AN INTERNATIONAL PERSPECTIVE, ENST 317 ENVIRONMENTAL POLICY AND REGULATION, MGMT 330 HEALTHCARE ADMINISTRATION, NURS 445 LEADERSHIP IN A GLOBAL WORLD, or PUBL 201 PRINCIPLES OF PUBLIC POLICY; one Social and Behavioral Science course: SCIN 310 AIDS: BIOLOGICAL, MEDICAL, SOCIAL PERSPECTIVES, SOCI 230 SOCIOLOGY OF HEALTH & MEDICINE, SWRK 230 AIDS: SOCIAL PERSPECTIVES, SWRK 328 COMMUNITY MENTAL HEALTH, PHLT 305 HEALTH AND WELLNESS, or PHLT 390 TOPICS; and one Global or Population Health course: ANTH 307 MEDICAL ANTHROPOLOGY, NURS 220 COMMUNITY HEALTH AND TRADITIONAL CHINESE MEDICINE, NURS 365 PUBLIC HEALTH IN WEST AFRICA, NURS 425 COMMUNITY CENTERED NURSING, PHLT 290 TOPICS, SOCI 309 FOOD AND POPULATION, or SPAN 311 SPANISH FOR HEALTH CARE AND HUMAN SERVICES PROFESSIONALS. [1]

BIOL 204 is 4 credits and requires BIOL 111 FUNDAMENTALS OF BIOLOGY I LECTURE. [3] PHLT 290 is 4 credits; no prerequisites are published. [4] NURS 425 is 4 credits; it has prerequisite and corequisite requirements. [7]

Sources: [1](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/programs/SN-MN-PHLT) [3](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/courses/BIOL204) [4](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/courses/PHLT290) [7](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/courses/NURS425)

In extraordinary circumstances a student can request an extension, up to the end of the following semester, on the Registrar's form with the student's signature and the faculty member's approval, due by the last day to resolve incompletes (Feb 12, 2027 for fall incompletes).

question: whats the max credits i can take in a semester and can i go over it
good_reply: 18 credits a semester. More needs a credit overload request through the Registrar (form), at extra cost; the GPA rule is 3.0 (the catalog says a student under 3.0 needs the advisor's approval first), and over 20 credits needs the school dean's approval.
must_not: Leaving out how to go over the limit. Invented people, numbers, rooms or dates.

body.answer:
Center for Student Success (Academic Advising): 18 credits per semester is typical. [9] A student can request more than the allotted 18 credits by applying for a credit overload. [9] A student must have above a 3.0 GPA or be a graduating senior to be granted the overload. [9] The credit overload request form is here: [https://www.ramapo.edu/registrar/credit-overload-request-form/](https://www.ramapo.edu/registrar/credit-overload-request-form/) [9]
Office of the Provost: A Fall and Spring A matriculated student who wishes to register for more than 18 credits per semester (at additional cost) must request that the Office of the Registrar raise their credit limit. [2] If the student has under a 3.0 cumulative GPA, the student must obtain approval to raise the credit limit from their academic advisor prior to making the request to the Office of the Registrar. [2] If the student is attempting to register for more than 20 credits, they must obtain approval from their school Dean. [2]
Registrar: The credit overload request form is used when an undergraduate student wishes to take more than 18 credits or a graduate student wishes to take more than the maximum for their program. [12] A credit overload is ONLY granted if the student has a 3.0 GPA or above. [12] Credit overloads will incur additional charges. [12]

- **Center for Student Success (Academic Advising)**: Phone: (201) 684-7441. Email: success@ramapo.edu. Office: D-207. [25]
- **Office of the Provost**: Phone: (201) 684-7330. Email: provost@ramapo.edu. Location: first floor of the Birch Mansion. [25]

Sources: [2](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/pages/R532kjMfIcfnIkM0srb3#credit-load) [9](https://www.ramapo.edu/studentsuccess/policies/) [12](https://www.ramapo.edu/registrar/credit-overload-request-form/) [25](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/)

question: i think my final grade is wrong, how do i appeal it and is there a deadline
good_reply: Within 20 calendar days after grades post, appeal in writing (email or certified letter) to the instructor with documentation; they have 15 days to decide. If no agreement, a written appeal to the dean of the school that sponsored the course within 20 days (15 days to decide), then a petition to the Office of the Provost within 20 days. Valid grounds: computational error, work not graded, a College policy violation (not wanting a higher GPA).
must_not: Stopping at the first step; no deadline. Invented people, numbers, rooms or dates.

body.answer:
That's stressful, but one bad grade doesn't decide everything. Talking with your professor and an advisor soon can really help.

Office of the Provost: You may appeal if you can document your case [2].
1. No later than twenty calendar days after the posting of grades, bring your appeal to the course instructor in writing by email or certified letter, with supporting documentation [3].
2. If you and the instructor cannot agree, submit a written appeal by email or certified letter, including pertinent course materials or course work, to the Dean of the academic unit which sponsored the course in question within twenty calendar days of the final determination conference [3].
3. If the Dean does not support your appeal, you may petition the Office of the Provost with a written statement by email or certified letter explaining your position and including contradictory evidence or information that had been unavailable [3]. Submit the petition within twenty calendar days of the Dean’s final, written determination [3].

**Office of the Provost**: Phone: (201) 684-7330. Email: provost@ramapo.edu. Location: first floor of the Birch Mansion. [31]

This office can help:
**Center for Student Success (Academic Advising)**: Phone: (201) 684-7441. Email: success@ramapo.edu. Office: D-207. [32]

pageFacts.question: i think my final grade is wrong, how do i appeal it and is there a deadline

facts.says: Circumstances for which students may appeal gradesGrade appeals will be considered only if a student can provide documentation supporting their case.

Circumstances that might justify a grade appeal include (but are not limited to): computational error; factual information not in evidence at the time the grade was posted (for example, an assignment that the student can document was submitted but was not graded by the course instructor and therefore not factored into the final grade); or an alleged violation of College Policy.

If circumstances such as those described above can be documented, the student may appeal a grade by taking the following steps: No later than twenty calendar days after the posting of grades, a student must bring their appeal to the attention of the course instructor in writing by email or certified letter.
Supporting documentation must be provided.
Both parties should make good faith efforts to share viewpoints and mediate differences of opinion.
Students and instructors have up to 15 calendar days to reach a determination of grade.

If a student and the course instructor cannot reach an agreement and a student wishes to further pursue a grade appeal, the student must present a written appeal (by email or certified letter), including pertinent course materials or course work, to the Dean of the academic unit which sponsored the course in question within twenty calendar days of the final determination conference between the student and the course instructor.
If the Dean renders an opinion which does not support the student’s grade appeal, the student may petition for a review by the Office of the Provost.

The petition is initiated by the submission of a written statement by the student, submitted by email or certified letter, that explains their position and includes any evidence that contradicts the Dean’s decision or contains information that had heretofore been unavailable.
Such a petition must be made within twenty calendar days of the final, written determination by the Dean.

pageFacts.question: i think my final grade is wrong, how do i appeal it and is there a deadline

facts.says: Circumstances for which students may appeal gradesGrade appeals will be considered only if a student can provide documentation supporting their case.

Circumstances that might justify a grade appeal include (but are not limited to): computational error; factual information not in evidence at the time the grade was posted (for example, an assignment that the student can document was submitted but was not graded by the course instructor and therefore not factored into the final grade); or an alleged violation of College Policy.

If circumstances such as those described above can be documented, the student may appeal a grade by taking the following steps: No later than twenty calendar days after the posting of grades, a student must bring their appeal to the attention of the course instructor in writing by email or certified letter.
Supporting documentation must be provided.
Both parties should make good faith efforts to share viewpoints and mediate differences of opinion.
Students and instructors have up to 15 calendar days to reach a determination of grade.

If a student and the course instructor cannot reach an agreement and a student wishes to further pursue a grade appeal, the student must present a written appeal (by email or certified letter), including pertinent course materials or course work, to the Dean of the academic unit which sponsored the course in question within twenty calendar days of the final determination conference between the student and the course instructor.
If the Dean renders an opinion which does not support the student’s grade appeal, the student may petition for a review by the Office of the Provost.

The petition is initiated by the submission of a written statement by the student, submitted by email or certified letter, that explains their position and includes any evidence that contradicts the Dean’s decision or contains information that had heretofore been unavailable.
Such a petition must be made within twenty calendar days of the final, written determination by the Dean.

question: if i drop a class and go part time will i lose my financial aid
good_reply: Aid is adjusted below full time (12 credits): federal aid needs at least 6 credits; going from 12 to 6 reduces a Pell Grant but federal loans can be kept; state aid may be canceled; Ramapo grants and scholarships (merit scholarships need 12 credits) may be reduced or taken away. Talk to Financial Aid before dropping.
must_not: Leading with "I can't see your records" instead of the rules (a short note at the end is fine). Invented people, numbers, rooms or dates.

body.answer:
It depends. Financial Aid says federal aid requires 6 credits in a semester; if you go from full time status 12 credits to part time status 6 credits your federal pell will be reduced but you can keep your federal loans. [1] NJ State aid (ie TAG, EOF, etc) requires full-time enrollment when the aid is fully disbursed to your account. [2] If you drop below full-time status, which is less than 12 credits, your Academic Scholarship or Ramapo grant may be taken away or reduced for the semester. [3] Contact the Office of Financial Aid before making a change that drops you below full-time status. [3]

**Financial Aid**: Phone: (201) 684-7549. Email: finaid@ramapo.edu. Office: E-210. [11]

Sources: [1](https://www.ramapo.edu/finaid/faqs/) [2](https://www.ramapo.edu/finaid/faqs/) [3](https://www.ramapo.edu/finaid/academic-merit-scholarships-terms-conditions/) [11](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/)

question: i have a medical condition, how can i request a housing accommodation
good_reply: Step 1: register with OSS (Application for Affiliation plus documentation from a licensed provider). Step 2: the Housing Accommodation Student Request Form and Provider Documentation Form. Step 3: meet Residence Life's deadlines. A committee (OSS, Residence Life, Health, Counseling) decides within 21 business days of complete documentation. OSS: 201-684-7514, oss@ramapo.edu, C-205.
must_not: Leaving out a step. Invented people, numbers, rooms or dates.

body.answer:
You can ask for support with that.

1. Office of Specialized Services (OSS): Register for affiliation with OSS first. [3]
2. Submit comprehensive disability documentation from a licensed physician, psychiatrist, psychologist, social worker, or certified learning disabilities specialist to establish eligibility and determine appropriate accommodations. [3]
3. If you are requesting only a strobe alarm, roll-in shower, wheelchair/mobility accessible residence hall, or 1st floor, you do not need to complete the Housing Accommodation Student or Provider Request Forms. [3]
4. See the Housing Accommodations webpage for more information and necessary forms: [https://www.ramapo.edu/oss/housing-accommodations/](https://www.ramapo.edu/oss/housing-accommodations/) [6]
5. For more information on registering, see “How To Request OSS Services”: [https://www.ramapo.edu/oss/how-to-request-oss-services/](https://www.ramapo.edu/oss/how-to-request-oss-services/) [3]

**Office of Specialized Services**: Phone: (201) 684-7514. Email: oss@ramapo.edu. Location: C-Wing, Room 205. [11]

Sources: [3](https://www.ramapo.edu/oss/housing-accommodations/) [6](https://www.ramapo.edu/oss/campus-accessibility-and-services-information/housing/) [11](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/)

citations.title: #1 - Register with the Office of Specialized Services

pageFacts.question: i have a medical condition, how can i request a housing accommodation

facts.says: Any resident, who is requesting specific housing accommodations, due to a medically related condition, will need to register with the Office of Specialized Services (OSS).
Please submit requests for housing accommodations no later than published deadlines.
Phone 201-684-7514 Email: oss@ramapo.edu www.ramapo.edu/oss
All students requesting a housing accommodation based on a disability must first register for affiliation with the Office of Specialized Services (OSS).
Check out our webpage “How To Request OSS Services” (https://www.ramapo.edu/oss/how-to-request-oss-services/) for more information.
Students must initiate contact with OSS in order to receive services or to arrange appropriate accommodations and/or academic adjustments.

Comprehensive documentation of a disability from a licensed physician, psychiatrist, psychologist, social worker, or certified learning disabilities specialist must be submitted in order to establish eligibility and to determine which accommodations and/or adjustments are appropriate for each student.

Note: Students requesting only a strobe alarm, roll-in shower, wheelchair/mobility accessible residence hall, or 1st floor do not need to complete the Housing Accommodation Student or Provider Request Forms, as below.
Students can expect a decision about their request within twenty one (21) business days of OSS receiving all requested documentation.
Please see our Housing Accommodations (https://www.ramapo.edu/oss/housing-accommodations/) webpage for more information and to find necessary forms.

question: i broke my wrist and cant write for a few weeks. can OSS help me with notes and exams
good_reply: Yes, OSS serves students with temporary disabilities such as a broken limb: submit the Application for Disability Support and current documentation, then an intake meeting with the OSS Director or Assistant Director authorizes accommodations. OSS: 201-684-7514, oss@ramapo.edu, C-205.
must_not: Saying OSS only helps permanent disabilities. Invented people, numbers, rooms or dates.

body.answer:
I'm sorry you're dealing with that, and I hope you feel better soon.

Yes. The Office of Specialized Services supports students with temporary disabilities; possible accommodations include notetakers, scribes, extended testing time, or alternative testing arrangements. [13][14]

- Schedule a meeting with your OSS Counselor on Connect and request a notetaker to review your semester accommodations. [4]
- Log into OSSOnline to select accommodations for your courses; your counselor will be notified to review and approve them. [7]
- Submit exam reservations through OSSOnline no later than 7 days before an on-campus exam and 14 days before an on-campus final. [8]

**Office of Specialized Services**: Phone: (201) 684-7514. Email: oss@ramapo.edu. Location: C-Wing, Room 205. [23]

This office can help:
**Health Services**: Phone: (201) 684-7536. Location: Near the campus South Gate entrance at the corner of Route 202 and Hornbeam Road. [24]

question: can i have an emotional support animal in my dorm, and how does approval work
good_reply: Call OSS at 201-684-7514 and meet with the OSS Director; documentation from a health care or mental health professional is needed; the animal may come only after OSS approval (Residence Life pets rule); it may be limited to defined areas, generally not academic or recreational buildings.
must_not: Invented people, numbers, rooms or dates.

body.answer:
Yes, you can have an emotional support animal in your dorm after approval through the Office of Specialized Services. [10] To qualify, a student with a disability must register with OSS, provide disability documentation demonstrating the animal’s benefits, and receive an accommodation permitting the animal on campus. [2] The request is reviewed by OSS staff and usually the Housing Accommodation Request Committee; they determine whether it is reasonable and may deny it if unreasonable or insufficiently documented. [5][8][6][4] If applicable, the College may ask about the animal’s age, size/breed to assess reasonableness. [7] The process takes time. [9] Call the Office of Specialized Services at 201-684-7514 to discuss your interest; interested students will be scheduled to meet with the OSS Director. [1][2] See the Emotional Support Animal Policy: [https://www.ramapo.edu/oss/campus-accessibility-and-services-information/service-support-animal-policy/](https://www.ramapo.edu/oss/campus-accessibility-and-services-information/service-support-animal-policy/) [3]

- **Office of the Provost**: Phone: (201) 684-7330. Email: provost@ramapo.edu. Location: first floor of the Birch Mansion. [27]
- **Office of Specialized Services**: Phone: (201) 684-7514. Email: oss@ramapo.edu. Location: C-Wing, Room 205. [27]

Sources: [1](https://www.ramapo.edu/oss/housing-accommodations/) [2](https://www.ramapo.edu/oss/campus-accessibility-and-services-information/service-support-animal-policy/) [3](https://www.ramapo.edu/oss/campus-accessibility-and-services-information/service-support-animal-policy/) [4](https://www.ramapo.edu/oss/housing-accommodations/) [5](https://www.ramapo.edu/oss/frequently-asked-questions/) [6](https://www.ramapo.edu/policies/policy/centers-institutes-guidelines/) [7](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/pages/R532kjMfIcfnIkM0srb3#academic-policy-approval-process) [8](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/pages/R532kjMfIcfnIkM0srb3#academic-policy-approval-process) [9](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/pages/R532kjMfIcfnIkM0srb3#academic-policy-approval-process) [10](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/pages/R532kjMfIcfnIkM0srb3#academic-policy-approval-process) [27](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/)

facts.says: Please call our office at 201-684-7514 to discuss your interest in having an Emotional Support Animal on campus.

When a student with a disability has registered with the Office of Specialized Services (OSS), provided disability documentation demonstrating the benefits provided by the emotional support animal, and been granted an accommodation permitting the presence of the emotional support animal on campus.
OSS and/or the Housing Accommodation Request Committee may deny a requested accommodation if it is unreasonable or insufficiently documented.
OSS together with the Housing Accommodation Request Committee shall determine if the requested accommodation is reasonable.
Regarding a request for an emotional support animal, if applicable the College may also inquire as to the age, size/breed of an animal in order to determine the reasonableness of this accommodation.
The request is then reviewed by the OSS staff and in most cases the Housing Accommodation Request Committee.
Time is needed for this process to be completed.
Emotional support animals, however, may be present after approval through the Office of Specialized Services (https://www.ramapo.edu/oss/service-support-animal-policy/).

question: i got a parking ticket. how do i pay or appeal it and how long do i have
good_reply: Appeal online within 20 days of the citation (appeal form; reviewed by the Parking Appeals Board). A citation not paid or appealed within 20 days gets a $5 late fee (another $5 after 28 days), and the right to appeal is lost after 20 days. Payment as the page says.
must_not: Leaving out the 20-day limit. Invented people, numbers, rooms or dates.

body.answer:
Public Safety: You have twenty (20) days from the issuance of a citation to submit an appeal online through the [Appeal Portal](https://cm.maxient.com/reportingform.php?RamapoCollege&layout_id=3). [1] Failure to file within twenty (20) days forfeits the right to appeal. [1] Citations not paid or appealed within 20 days are subject to a $5 late fee. [3] The ability to appeal is forfeit if the appeal is not submitted within 20 days. [3] A second $5 late fee may be assessed after 28 days. [3]

To pay:
1. Use the [Payment Portal](https://rcnjpublicsafety.omnigo.one/CESIReportExec/OCP/Main.aspx). Enter Citation # and Fine Amount, search for the citation, select your citation, and follow the field required. [4]
2. Select Payment Method. Once processed, your citation will be emailed to you to say that it is paid. [4]

- **Public Safety (Non-Emergency)**: Phone: (201) 684-7432. Email: publicsafety@ramapo.edu. Office: C-102. [23]
- **Public Safety (Emergency)**: Phone: (201) 684-6666. Email: publicsafety@ramapo.edu. Office: C-102. [23]

Sources: [1](https://www.ramapo.edu/publicsafety/vehicle-citation-information/) [3](https://www.ramapo.edu/publicsafety/parking-regulations/) [4](https://www.ramapo.edu/publicsafety/vehicle-citation-information/) [23](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/)

question: how do i pay my student account bill online
good_reply: Log in to RCNJ Experience (Web Self-Service), open the Student Account Info card, then Bill & Payment Suite and Make Payment; pay by electronic check (checking/savings) or credit/debit card via PayPath. Bills are eBills only; a monthly payment plan exists. Student Accounts: studentaccts@ramapo.edu, (201) 684-7495.
must_not: Anything about the Accounting program.

body.answer:
1. Student Accounts: Log into RCNJ Experience (Web Self-Service) ([https://experience.elluciancloud.com/rconj/](https://experience.elluciancloud.com/rconj/)), locate the Student Account Info card, click Bill & Payment Suite, then click the Make Payment tab at top of page. [6]
2. Select the term you wish to make payment for, click Continue, choose Credit Card via PayPath from the Payment Method drop down, then click Select. [6]
3. Verify or modify the payment amount, click Continue to PayPath, read the non-refundable PayPath service fee disclaimer on the Welcome to the PayPath Payment Service! Screen, then click Continue. [6]
4. Review payment amount information, click Continue, enter all Credit/Debit Card Billing Information and click Continue. Review your entries; if any data is incorrect, click Change Information. If you do not wish to have your transaction processed, click Cancel. Click Submit to submit your payment; by submitting, you accept the non-refundable service fee. Print the Payment Confirmation Page for your records. The College reserves the right to change costs, dates and procedures at its discretion. [6]

**Student Accounts**: Phone: (201) 684-7495. Email: studentaccts@ramapo.edu. Location: D-Wing, First Floor. [11]

Sources: [6](https://www.ramapo.edu/student-accounts/methods/) [11](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/)

3. Center for Student Involvement: Once the College recognizes the organization, it is eligible to receive financial support from the Student Activities Allocations Committee. [4]

question: tell me about the MPP
good_reply: The Public Policy MPP (Master of Public Policy) in the School of Social Sciences and Social Work, from its catalog description. The Public Policy 4+1 may be added.
must_not: Saying there is no such program; describing another program.

body.answer:
The Public Policy MPP is a Master of Public Policy in the School of Social Sciences and Social Work. It studies how governmental laws and policies shape human lives and develops research, quantitative and qualitative methods, and skills for work with or for public institutions. Public Policy 4+1 and Public Policy Minor are also published. [1]

Requirements: all seven required courses: PUBL 600 THE POLITICS OF POLICYMAKING; PUBL 601 FEDERAL PUBLIC POLICY & GOVERNANCE; PUBL 602 STATE & LOCAL PUBLIC POLICY; PUBL 616 ECONOMETRICS AND ANALYSIS; PUBL 618 PUBLIC MANAGEMENT; PUBL 621 POLITICAL ECONOMY; PUBL 705 PUBLIC POLICY INTERNSHIP. Select 3 (at least 3) electives: ACCT 502 GOVERNMENT AND NOT-FOR-PROFIT ACCOUNTING; ACCT 625 INTERNATIONAL ACCOUNTING; BADM 501 DATA ANALYTICS; BADM 503 BUSINESS LAW, ETHICS & REGULATORY PRONOUNCEMENTS; DATA 601 INTRODUCTION TO DATA SCIENCE; DATA 670 DATA VISUALIZATION; MATH 570 APPLIED STATISTICS; MATH 685 INTRODUCTION TO EXPERIMENTAL DESIGN; MBAD 610 BECOMING A 21ST CENTURY LEADER; MBAD 625 CRISIS & CHANGE MANAGEMENT; NURS 660 LEADERSHIP AND INNOVATION IN HEALTHCARE; NURS 670 HEALTHCARE ECONOMICS AND FINANCE; NURS 808 HEALTH POLICY LEADERSHIP; MSWK 505 SOCIAL WELFARE PROGRAMS AND POLICIES I; MSWK 507 CULTURAL DIVERSITY, RACISM, OPPRESSION AND PRIVILEGE; MSWK 604 ADVANCED SOCIAL POLICY; MSWK 610 PUBLIC HEALTH IN WEST AFRICA; MSWK 670 SOCIAL WELFARE POLICIES IN HEALTH AND MENTAL HEALTH. [1]

Graduate Admissions lists one professional or academic recommendation (waived for current Ramapo students graduating in 2027 and recent graduates from 2025 and 2026); enter references’ names and contact information in “Recommendations” in the online application, and Ramapo sends an automated request so references can upload through the portal. Also required: a 400-word personal statement on interest, fit with intellectual development, and expected accomplishments, and a resume. [6]

**Graduate Admissions**: Phone: (201) 684-7270. Email: graduate@ramapo.edu. Location: McBride House. [15]

Sources: [1](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/programs/SO-MPP-PBPL) [6](https://www.ramapo.edu/graduate/requirements/) [15](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/)

question: what's the RN to BSN
good_reply: The Nursing RN to BSN track, for registered nurses with an associate's degree or diploma who return for the BSN; one of three BSN tracks (generic, accelerated, RN to BSN); accredited by ACEN.
must_not: Invented people, numbers, rooms or dates.

body.answer:
The Nursing RN to BSN is a Bachelor of Science in Nursing track for registered nurses with an Associate’s degree or Diploma in nursing. Students transfer credits from their initial nursing program and complete Ramapo’s general education and nursing requirements. Ramapo’s nursing programs are accredited by the Accreditation Commission for Education in Nursing (ACEN). Diploma-program graduates receive 30 credits for diploma nursing courses after satisfactory completion of their first two BSN nursing courses. [1]

Requirements: one course from MATH 108 Elementary Probability and Statistics, PSYC 242 Statistics, or SOCI 308 Data Analysis in Sociology; all RN to BSN Professional Core courses: NURS 312 Nursing Informatics, NURS 316 Pathophysiology, NURS 325 Nursing Research and Evidence Based Practice, NURS 330 Health Assessment Across the Lifespan, NURS 425 Community Centered Nursing, NURS 445 Leadership in a Global World, and NURS 460 Clinical Management; and one elective. Students should consult their Nursing advisor for elective course options. [1]

Also published: Nursing Accelerated BSN, Nursing Generic BSN, and Nursing MSN. [1]

Sources: [1](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/programs/SN-BSN-NURS)

question: how many classes is the public health minor and which ones count
good_reply: Five courses: BIOL 204 Epidemiology, plus one each from statistics/research methods, health policy and management, social and behavioral science, and global or population health, with examples from each list.
must_not: Leaving out a course group. Invented people, numbers, rooms or dates.

body.answer:
The Public Health Minor consists of five courses (20 credits). [1]

You must take BIOL 204 EPIDEMIOLOGY. [1] It is 4 credits and requires BIOL 111 FUNDAMENTALS OF BIOLOGY I LECTURE. [3]

Choose one Statistics or Research Methods course: BADM 225 MANAGEMENT STATISTICS; ENSC 345 RESEARCH DESIGN & STATISTICS; MATH 370 APPLIED STATISTICS; NURS 325 NURSING RESEARCH AND EVIDENCE BASED PRACTICE; PSYC 242 STATISTICS; PSYC 303 RESEARCH METHODS IN PSYCHOLOGY; SOCI 307 SOCIAL RESEARCH WITH COMPUTERS; or SWRK 307 SOCIAL WORK RESEARCH METHODS. [1]

Choose one Health Policy and Management course: COMM 383 THEORY AND PRACTICE OF HEALTH COMMUNICATION; ECON 332 HEALTH ECONOMICS: AN INTERNATIONAL PERSPECTIVE; ENST 317 ENVIRONMENTAL POLICY AND REGULATION; MGMT 330 HEALTHCARE ADMINISTRATION; NURS 445 LEADERSHIP IN A GLOBAL WORLD; or PUBL 201 PRINCIPLES OF PUBLIC POLICY. [1]

Choose one Social and Behavioral Science course: SCIN 310 AIDS: BIOLOGICAL, MEDICAL, SOCIAL PERSPECTIVES; SOCI 230 SOCIOLOGY OF HEALTH & MEDICINE; SWRK 230 AIDS: SOCIAL PERSPECTIVES; SWRK 328 COMMUNITY MENTAL HEALTH; PHLT 305 HEALTH AND WELLNESS; or PHLT 390 TOPICS. [1] PHLT 305 and PHLT 390 are 4 credits each and have no published prerequisites. [5][6]

Choose one Global or Population Health course: ANTH 307 MEDICAL ANTHROPOLOGY; NURS 220 COMMUNITY HEALTH AND TRADITIONAL CHINESE MEDICINE; NURS 365 PUBLIC HEALTH IN WEST AFRICA; NURS 425 COMMUNITY CENTERED NURSING; PHLT 290 TOPICS; SOCI 309 FOOD AND POPULATION; or SPAN 311 SPANISH FOR HEALTH CARE AND HUMAN SERVICES PROFESSIONALS. [1] PHLT 290 is 4 credits and has no published prerequisites. [4]

PHLT 300 and ENST 355 are not listed in this minor's requirements. [1]

Sources: [1](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/programs/SN-MN-PHLT) [3](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/courses/BIOL204) [4](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/courses/PHLT290) [5](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/courses/PHLT390) [6](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/courses/PHLT305)

question: what happens if i take an incomplete and don't finish the work in time? can i get more time
good_reply: An I needs the instructor's approval and at least two-thirds of the course done. Work not finished by the date on the academic calendar turns the I into an F. In extraordinary circumstances a student can request an extension, up to the end of the following semester, on the Registrar's form with the student's signature and the faculty member's approval, due by the last day to resolve incompletes (Feb 12, 2027 for fall incompletes).
must_not: Leaving out that it becomes an F, or that an extension exists. Invented people, numbers, rooms or dates.

body.answer:
The Fall 2026 academic calendar lists [21]:
- Friday, October 16, 2026: Session I Courses - Last Day to Request an Incomplete ("I" Grade) (already passed)
- Tuesday, December 15, 2026: Full and Session II Courses - Last Day to Request an Incomplete ("I" Grade)

Yes—in extraordinary circumstances, you may request an incomplete extension [6]. If you do not satisfactorily complete the work by the completion date on the Incomplete Form or academic calendar (the earlier date applies), your grade changes to F; if you complete it by then, the assigned grade replaces I [4].

1. Registrar: Complete the Incomplete Form with your instructor. Review the Academic Calendar ([https://www.ramapo.edu/academic-calendars/](https://www.ramapo.edu/academic-calendars/)) for Incomplete Deadlines, and submit the form to the Office of the Registrar: reg@ramapo.edu [4].
2. Registrar: Obtain the incomplete extension form from the Office of the Registrar; it requires your signature and faculty approval [6].
3. Registrar: Submit the extension by the last day to resolve an incomplete grade shown on the Academic Calendar. An extension can last only through the end of the semester after the semester the I was given [6].

**Registrar**: Phone: (201) 684-7695. Email: reg@ramapo.edu. Office: D-224. [22]

Sources: [4](https://www.ramapo.edu/registrar/grading-options/) [6](https://www.ramapo.edu/registrar/grading-options/) [21](https://www.ramapo.edu/academic-calendars/) [22](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/)

facts.says: If the work is completed by the completion date indicated on the Incomplete Form or the academic calendar (the earliest date will be honored), the grade assigned replaces the I. If the work is not satisfactorily completed by the completion date the grade is changed to F. Requesting an Incomplete Grade: Review the Academic Calendar (https://www.ramapo.edu/academic-calendars/) for Incomplete Deadlines The Incomplete Form must be completed by the student and the instructor.
The form must be submitted to the Office of the Registrar: reg@ramapo.edu (mailto:reg@ramapo.edu).
In extraordinary circumstances a student may request an incomplete extension.
The incomplete may only be extended until the end of the semester following the semester the incomplete grade was given.
The incomplete extension form must be obtained from the Office of the Registrar and requires the student’s signature and the faculty’s approval.
The deadline to submit the extension to the Office of the Registrar is the last day to resolve an incomplete grade as posted on the Academic Calendar.

question: whats the max credits i can take in a semester and can i go over it
good_reply: 18 credits a semester. More needs a credit overload request through the Registrar (form), at extra cost; the GPA rule is 3.0 (the catalog says a student under 3.0 needs the advisor's approval first), and over 20 credits needs the school dean's approval.
must_not: Leaving out how to go over the limit. Invented people, numbers, rooms or dates.

body.answer:
Center for Student Success (Academic Advising): A student is typically permitted to take up to 18 credits per semester, but can request more by applying for a credit overload. [9]
Office of the Provost: For Fall and Spring, a matriculated student wishing to register for more than 18 credits must request that the Office of the Registrar raise the limit, at additional cost. [2] If the student has under a 3.0 cumulative GPA, approval from their academic advisor is required before making that request. [2] More than 20 credits requires approval from the school Dean. [2]
Registrar: A credit overload is ONLY granted if the student has a 3.0 GPA or above. [12]

- **Center for Student Success (Academic Advising)**: Phone: (201) 684-7441. Email: success@ramapo.edu. Office: D-207. [25]
- **Office of the Provost**: Phone: (201) 684-7330. Email: provost@ramapo.edu. Location: first floor of the Birch Mansion. [25]

question: i think my final grade is wrong, how do i appeal it and is there a deadline
good_reply: Within 20 calendar days after grades post, appeal in writing (email or certified letter) to the instructor with documentation; they have 15 days to decide. If no agreement, a written appeal to the dean of the school that sponsored the course within 20 days (15 days to decide), then a petition to the Office of the Provost within 20 days. Valid grounds: computational error, work not graded, a College policy violation (not wanting a higher GPA).
must_not: Stopping at the first step; no deadline. Invented people, numbers, rooms or dates.

body.answer:
That's stressful, but one bad grade doesn't decide everything. Talking with your professor and an advisor soon can really help.

The Office of the Provost sets the first deadline at no later than twenty calendar days after grades are posted. [3]

1. Bring your appeal to the course instructor in writing by email or certified letter, and provide supporting documentation. [3]
2. If you and the instructor cannot agree, send a written appeal by email or certified letter, with pertinent course materials or course work, to the Dean of the academic unit that sponsored the course within twenty calendar days of the final determination conference. [7]
3. If the Dean’s opinion does not support your appeal, you may petition for a review by the Office of the Provost. [10]

**Office of the Provost**: Phone: (201) 684-7330. Email: provost@ramapo.edu. Location: first floor of the Birch Mansion. [31]

This office can help:
**Center for Student Success (Academic Advising)**: Phone: (201) 684-7441. Email: success@ramapo.edu. Office: D-207. [32]

Sources: [3](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/pages/R532kjMfIcfnIkM0srb3#student-appeals-of-an-academic-nature) [7](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/pages/R532kjMfIcfnIkM0srb3#student-appeals-of-an-academic-nature) [10](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/pages/R532kjMfIcfnIkM0srb3#academic-integrity) [31](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/) [32](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/)
