pageFacts.question: i think my final grade is wrong, how do i appeal it and is there a deadline

facts.says: Circumstances for which students may appeal gradesGrade appeals will be considered only if a student can provide documentation supporting their case.

Circumstances that might justify a grade appeal include (but are not limited to): computational error; factual information not in evidence at the time the grade was posted (for example, an assignment that the student can document was submitted but was not graded by the course instructor and therefore not factored into the final grade); or an alleged violation of College Policy.

If circumstances such as those described above can be documented, the student may appeal a grade by taking the following steps: No later than twenty calendar days after the posting of grades, a student must bring their appeal to the attention of the course instructor in writing by email or certified letter.
Supporting documentation must be provided.
Both parties should make good faith efforts to share viewpoints and mediate differences of opinion.
Students and instructors have up to 15 calendar days to reach a determination of grade.

If a student and the course instructor cannot reach an agreement and a student wishes to further pursue a grade appeal, the student must present a written appeal (by email or certified letter), including pertinent course materials or course work, to the Dean of the academic unit which sponsored the course in question within twenty calendar days of the final determination conference between the student and the course instructor.

The Dean will confer with the student and the course instructor, jointly or independently as they see fit, review pertinent documents and course materials, and confer with other faculty or administrative staff members as appropriate.
The Deans have 15 calendar days to make this determination.
If the Dean renders an opinion which does not support the student’s grade appeal, the student may petition for a review by the Office of the Provost.

question: if i drop a class and go part time will i lose my financial aid
good_reply: Aid is adjusted below full time (12 credits): federal aid needs at least 6 credits; going from 12 to 6 reduces a Pell Grant but federal loans can be kept; state aid may be canceled; Ramapo grants and scholarships (merit scholarships need 12 credits) may be reduced or taken away. Talk to Financial Aid before dropping.
must_not: Leading with "I can't see your records" instead of the rules (a short note at the end is fine). Invented people, numbers, rooms or dates.

body.answer:
It depends. Financial Aid says federal aid should not be affected if you remain enrolled for 6 or more credits [2]. If you drop from 12 credits to 6, your federal Pell will be reduced, but you can keep your federal loans [1]. NJ State aid requires full-time enrollment when the aid is fully disbursed to your account [2]. Your Academic Scholarship or Ramapo grant may be reduced or taken away if you drop below 12 credits [3].

**Financial Aid**: Phone: (201) 684-7549. Email: finaid@ramapo.edu. Office: E-210. [11]

Sources: [1](https://www.ramapo.edu/finaid/faqs/) [2](https://www.ramapo.edu/finaid/faqs/) [3](https://www.ramapo.edu/finaid/academic-merit-scholarships-terms-conditions/) [11](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/)

question: i have a medical condition, how can i request a housing accommodation
good_reply: Step 1: register with OSS (Application for Affiliation plus documentation from a licensed provider). Step 2: the Housing Accommodation Student Request Form and Provider Documentation Form. Step 3: meet Residence Life's deadlines. A committee (OSS, Residence Life, Health, Counseling) decides within 21 business days of complete documentation. OSS: 201-684-7514, oss@ramapo.edu, C-205.
must_not: Leaving out a step. Invented people, numbers, rooms or dates.

body.answer:
You can ask for support with that.

**Housing & Residence Life**
Any resident, who is requesting specific housing accommodations, due to a medically related condition, will need to register with the Office of Specialized Services (OSS). Please submit requests for housing accommodations no later than published deadlines. Phone 201-684-7514 Email: oss@ramapo.edu www.ramapo.edu/oss. [1]

**Office of Specialized Services**
1. All students requesting a housing accommodation based on a disability must first register for affiliation with the Office of Specialized Services (OSS). [3]
Check out our webpage “How To Request OSS Services” ([https://www.ramapo.edu/oss/how-to-request-oss-services/](https://www.ramapo.edu/oss/how-to-request-oss-services/)) for more information. Students must initiate contact with OSS in order to receive services or to arrange appropriate accommodations and/or academic adjustments. [3]
2. Comprehensive documentation of a disability from a licensed physician, psychiatrist, psychologist, social worker, or certified learning disabilities specialist must be submitted in order to establish eligibility and to determine which accommodations and/or adjustments are appropriate for each student. [3]
Students only need to complete a request for disability support form. [3]
Students can expect a decision about their request within twenty one (21) business days of OSS receiving all requested documentation. [4]
Once approved, OSS will work with Residence Life on having the student appropriately placed.[https://www.ramapo.edu/oss/housing-accommodations/](https://www.ramapo.edu/oss/housing-accommodations/) Q: How can I be placed in a residence hall that has a kitchen? [5]

- **Housing & Residence Life**: Phone: (201) 684-7461. Email: reslife@ramapo.edu. [11]
- **Office of Specialized Services**: Phone: (201) 684-7514. Email: oss@ramapo.edu. Location: C-Wing, Room 205. [11]

Sources: [1](https://www.ramapo.edu/reslife/apply/) [3](https://www.ramapo.edu/oss/housing-accommodations/) [4](https://www.ramapo.edu/oss/housing-accommodations/) [5](https://www.ramapo.edu/oss/frequently-asked-questions/) [11](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/)

question: can i have an emotional support animal in my dorm, and how does approval work
good_reply: Call OSS at 201-684-7514 and meet with the OSS Director; documentation from a health care or mental health professional is needed; the animal may come only after OSS approval (Residence Life pets rule); it may be limited to defined areas, generally not academic or recreational buildings.
must_not: Invented people, numbers, rooms or dates.

body.answer:
Yes, but an emotional support animal may be in campus housing only after approval through the Office of Specialized Services (OSS). [12] Please call the Office of Specialized Services at 201-684-7514 to discuss your interest; interested students will be scheduled to meet with the OSS Director. [1] To qualify, you must register with OSS, provide disability documentation showing the animal’s benefits, and receive an accommodation permitting the animal on campus. [2] OSS and/or the Housing Accommodation Request Committee may deny a request if it is unreasonable or insufficiently documented; together, they determine whether it is reasonable. [4] The College may ask about the animal’s age, size/breed, if applicable. [4] OSS staff and, in most cases, the Housing Accommodation Request Committee review the request, and the process takes time. [5] Once approved, OSS works with Residence Life on placement. [5]

- **Housing & Residence Life**: Phone: (201) 684-7461. Email: reslife@ramapo.edu. [27]
- **Office of Specialized Services**: Phone: (201) 684-7514. Email: oss@ramapo.edu. Location: C-Wing, Room 205. [27]

Sources: [1](https://www.ramapo.edu/oss/housing-accommodations/) [2](https://www.ramapo.edu/oss/campus-accessibility-and-services-information/service-support-animal-policy/) [4](https://www.ramapo.edu/oss/housing-accommodations/) [5](https://www.ramapo.edu/oss/frequently-asked-questions/) [12](https://www.ramapo.edu/reslife/gtcl/) [27](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/)

question: i got a parking ticket. how do i pay or appeal it and how long do i have
good_reply: Appeal online within 20 days of the citation (appeal form; reviewed by the Parking Appeals Board). A citation not paid or appealed within 20 days gets a $5 late fee (another $5 after 28 days), and the right to appeal is lost after 20 days. Payment as the page says.
must_not: Leaving out the 20-day limit. Invented people, numbers, rooms or dates.

body.answer:
You have 20 days from the citation’s issuance to appeal; after 20 days, the right to appeal is forfeited and an unpaid or unappealed citation is subject to a $5 late fee. A second $5 late fee may be assessed after 28 days. [1][2][3][4][5]

Public Safety:
1. To appeal, submit an online appeal within twenty (20) days using the [appeal portal](https://cm.maxient.com/reportingform.php?RamapoCollege&layout_id=3). [1]
2. To pay, use the [payment portal](https://rcnjpublicsafety.omnigo.one/CESIReportExec/OCP/Main.aspx). Enter Citation # and Fine Amount, search for the citation, select it, and follow the required fields. [6]
3. Select Payment Method. Once processed, your citation will be emailed to you to say that it is paid. [7]

- **Public Safety (Non-Emergency)**: Phone: (201) 684-7432. Email: publicsafety@ramapo.edu. Office: C-102. [23]
- **Public Safety (Emergency)**: Phone: (201) 684-6666. Email: publicsafety@ramapo.edu. Office: C-102. [23]

Sources: [1](https://www.ramapo.edu/publicsafety/vehicle-citation-information/) [2](https://www.ramapo.edu/publicsafety/parking-regulations/) [3](https://www.ramapo.edu/publicsafety/parking-regulations/) [4](https://www.ramapo.edu/publicsafety/vehicle-citation-information/) [5](https://www.ramapo.edu/publicsafety/how-to-apply-for-a-parking-permit/) [6](https://www.ramapo.edu/policies/policy/1167/) [7](https://www.ramapo.edu/policies/policy/1167/) [23](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/)

facts.says: How to Appeal Your Parking Citation Click Here to Go to the Appeal Portal (https://cm.maxient.com/reportingform.php?RamapoCollege&layout_id=3) Appeals are input online via the form An online appeal by the owner/driver must be made within twenty (20) days of the issuance of a citation.
Failure to file the appeal within twenty (20) days constitutes forfeiture of the right to appeal.
IMPORTANT CONSIDERATIONS: Citations not paid or appealed within 20 days are subject to a $5 late fee.
The ability to appeal is forfeit if the appeal is not submitted within 20 days.
A second $5 late fee may be assessed after 28 days.

How to Pay for Your Parking Citation Online Click Here to Go to the Payment Portal (https://rcnjpublicsafety.omnigo.one/CESIReportExec/OCP/Main.aspx) Citations are paid online using the portal Enter Citation # and Fine Amount Search for Citation Select your Citation and follow the field required.
Select Payment Method Once processed your citation will be emailed to you to say that it is paid

question: how do i pay my student account bill online
good_reply: Log in to RCNJ Experience (Web Self-Service), open the Student Account Info card, then Bill & Payment Suite and Make Payment; pay by electronic check (checking/savings) or credit/debit card via PayPath. Bills are eBills only; a monthly payment plan exists. Student Accounts: studentaccts@ramapo.edu, (201) 684-7495.
must_not: Anything about the Accounting program.

body.answer:
Student Accounts:
1. Log into RCNJ Experience (Web Self-Service) ([https://experience.elluciancloud.com/rconj/](https://experience.elluciancloud.com/rconj/)), locate the Student Account Info card, click Bill & Payment Suite, then click the Make Payment tab at the top. Select the term, click Continue, choose Credit Card via PayPath from the Payment Method drop-down, then click Select. Verify or modify the payment amount and click Continue to PayPath. Read the non-refundable PayPath service fee disclaimer on the Welcome to the PayPath Payment Service! Screen, then click Continue. [6]
2. Review the payment amount and click Continue. Enter all Credit/Debit Card Billing Information and click Continue; review the displayed information, including the service fee amount charged by PayPath. [6]
3. Review your entries. If anything is incorrect, click Change Information; to cancel, click Cancel. Click Submit to submit your payment. By submitting, you accept the non-refundable service fee. Print the Payment Confirmation Page for your records. The College reserves the right to change costs, dates and procedures at its discretion. [6]

**Student Accounts**: Phone: (201) 684-7495. Email: studentaccts@ramapo.edu. Location: D-Wing, First Floor. [11]

Sources: [6](https://www.ramapo.edu/student-accounts/methods/) [11](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/)

question: tell me about the MPP
good_reply: The Public Policy MPP (Master of Public Policy) in the School of Social Sciences and Social Work, from its catalog description. The Public Policy 4+1 may be added.

body.answer:
The Public Policy MPP is a Master of Public Policy in the School of Social Sciences and Social Work. It focuses on how government laws and policies shape people’s lives and trains students in research methods and skills for work with or for public institutions. [1]

Requirements: PUBL 600 THE POLITICS OF POLICYMAKING; PUBL 601 FEDERAL PUBLIC POLICY & GOVERNANCE; PUBL 602 STATE & LOCAL PUBLIC POLICY; PUBL 616 ECONOMETRICS AND ANALYSIS; PUBL 618 PUBLIC MANAGEMENT; PUBL 621 POLITICAL ECONOMY; PUBL 705 PUBLIC POLICY INTERNSHIP; plus 3 electives (at least 3) from: ACCT 502 GOVERNMENT AND NOT-FOR-PROFIT ACCOUNTING; ACCT 625 INTERNATIONAL ACCOUNTING; BADM 501 DATA ANALYTICS; BADM 503 BUSINESS LAW, ETHICS & REGULATORY PRONOUNCEMENTS; DATA 601 INTRODUCTION TO DATA SCIENCE; DATA 670 DATA VISUALIZATION; MATH 570 APPLIED STATISTICS; MATH 685 INTRODUCTION TO EXPERIMENTAL DESIGN; MBAD 610 BECOMING A 21ST CENTURY LEADER; MBAD 625 CRISIS & CHANGE MANAGEMENT; NURS 660 LEADERSHIP AND INNOVATION IN HEALTHCARE; NURS 670 HEALTHCARE ECONOMICS AND FINANCE; NURS 808 HEALTH POLICY LEADERSHIP; MSWK 505 SOCIAL WELFARE PROGRAMS AND POLICIES I; MSWK 507 CULTURAL DIVERSITY, RACISM, OPPRESSION AND PRIVILEGE; MSWK 604 ADVANCED SOCIAL POLICY; MSWK 610 PUBLIC HEALTH IN WEST AFRICA; MSWK 670 SOCIAL WELFARE POLICIES IN HEALTH AND MENTAL HEALTH. [1]

Also published: Public Policy 4+1 and Public Policy Minor. [1]

Graduate Admissions lists one professional or academic recommendation (enter references in “Recommendations” in the online application; Ramapo sends an automated request and references upload through the application portal). This is waived for current Ramapo students graduating in 2027 and recent graduates from 2025 and 2026. It also lists a 400-word personal statement about your interest, intellectual development, and goals, and a resume. [6]

**Graduate Admissions**: Phone: (201) 684-7270. Email: graduate@ramapo.edu. Location: McBride House. [12]

Sources: [1](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/programs/SO-MPP-PBPL) [6](https://www.ramapo.edu/graduate/requirements/) [12](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/)

question: what's the RN to BSN
good_reply: The Nursing RN to BSN track, for registered nurses with an associate's degree or diploma who return for the BSN; one of three BSN tracks (generic, accelerated, RN to BSN); accredited by ACEN.
must_not: Invented people, numbers, rooms or dates.

body.answer:
The Nursing RN to BSN is a Bachelor of Science in Nursing track for registered nurses prepared at the Associate’s degree or Diploma level. Students transfer credits from their initial nursing program and complete Ramapo’s general education and nursing requirements. Diploma-program graduates receive 30 credits for diploma nursing courses after satisfactory completion of their first two BSN nursing courses. Ramapo’s nursing programs are accredited by the Accreditation Commission for Education in Nursing (ACEN). [1]

Requirements: Select 1 math course: MATH 108 ELEMENTARY PROBABILITY AND STATISTICS; PSYC 242 STATISTICS; or SOCI 308 DATA ANALYSIS IN SOCIOLOGY. Complete all RN to BSN Professional Core courses: NURS 312 NURSING INFORMATICS; NURS 316 PATHOPHYSIOLOGY; NURS 325 NURSING RESEARCH AND EVIDENCE BASED PRACTICE; NURS 330 HEALTH ASSESSMENT ACROSS THE LIFESPAN; NURS 425 COMMUNITY CENTERED NURSING; NURS 445 LEADERSHIP IN A GLOBAL WORLD; and NURS 460 CLINICAL MANAGEMENT. Select 1 elective; students should consult their Nursing advisor for elective course options. [1]

Also published: Nursing Accelerated BSN, Nursing Generic BSN, and Nursing MSN. [1]

Sources: [1](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/programs/SN-BSN-NURS)

question: how many classes is the public health minor and which ones count
good_reply: Five courses: BIOL 204 Epidemiology, plus one each from statistics/research methods, health policy and management, social and behavioral science, and global or population health, with examples from each list.
must_not: Leaving out a course group. Invented people, numbers, rooms or dates.

body.answer:
The Public Health Minor consists of five courses (20 credits). [1]

Required: BIOL 204 EPIDEMIOLOGY. [1]
Choose one from each group: [1]
• Statistics or Research Methods: BADM 225 MANAGEMENT STATISTICS; ENSC 345 RESEARCH DESIGN & STATISTICS; MATH 370 APPLIED STATISTICS; NURS 325 NURSING RESEARCH AND EVIDENCE BASED PRACTICE; PSYC 242 STATISTICS; PSYC 303 RESEARCH METHODS IN PSYCHOLOGY; SOCI 307 SOCIAL RESEARCH WITH COMPUTERS; or SWRK 307 SOCIAL WORK RESEARCH METHODS. [1]
• Health Policy and Management: COMM 383 THEORY AND PRACTICE OF HEALTH COMMUNICATION; ECON 332 HEALTH ECONOMICS: AN INTERNATIONAL PERSPECTIVE; ENST 317 ENVIRONMENTAL POLICY AND REGULATION; MGMT 330 HEALTHCARE ADMINISTRATION; NURS 445 LEADERSHIP IN A GLOBAL WORLD; or PUBL 201 PRINCIPLES OF PUBLIC POLICY. [1]
• Social and Behavioral Science: SCIN 310 AIDS: BIOLOGICAL, MEDICAL, SOCIAL PERSPECTIVES; SOCI 230 SOCIOLOGY OF HEALTH & MEDICINE; SWRK 230 AIDS: SOCIAL PERSPECTIVES; SWRK 328 COMMUNITY MENTAL HEALTH; PHLT 305 HEALTH AND WELLNESS; or PHLT 390 TOPICS. [1]
• Global or Population Health: ANTH 307 MEDICAL ANTHROPOLOGY; NURS 220 COMMUNITY HEALTH AND TRADITIONAL CHINESE MEDICINE; NURS 365 PUBLIC HEALTH IN WEST AFRICA; NURS 425 COMMUNITY CENTERED NURSING; PHLT 290 TOPICS; SOCI 309 FOOD AND POPULATION; or SPAN 311 SPANISH FOR HEALTH CARE AND HUMAN SERVICES PROFESSIONALS. [1]
BIOL 204 is 4 credits and requires BIOL 111 FUNDAMENTALS OF BIOLOGY I LECTURE. [4]

question: what happens if i take an incomplete and don't finish the work in time? can i get more time
good_reply: An I needs the instructor's approval and at least two-thirds of the course done. Work not finished by the date on the academic calendar turns the I into an F. In extraordinary circumstances a student can request an extension, up to the end of the following semester, on the Registrar's form with the student's signature and the faculty member's approval, due by the last day to resolve incompletes (Feb 12, 2027 for fall incompletes).
must_not: Leaving out that it becomes an F, or that an extension exists. Invented people, numbers, rooms or dates.

body.answer:
The Fall 2026 academic calendar lists [21]:
- Friday, October 16, 2026: Session I Courses - Last Day to Request an Incomplete ("I" Grade) (already passed)
- Tuesday, December 15, 2026: Full and Session II Courses - Last Day to Request an Incomplete ("I" Grade)

**Registrar**
If the work is completed by the completion date indicated on the Incomplete Form or the academic calendar (the earliest date will be honored), the grade assigned replaces the I. If the work is not satisfactorily completed by the completion date the grade is changed to F. Requesting an Incomplete Grade: Review the Academic Calendar ([https://www.ramapo.edu/academic-calendars/](https://www.ramapo.edu/academic-calendars/)) for Incomplete Deadlines The Incomplete Form must be completed by the student and the instructor. The form must be submitted to the Office of the Registrar: reg@ramapo.edu (mailto:reg@ramapo.edu). [4]
In extraordinary circumstances a student may request an incomplete extension. The incomplete may only be extended until the end of the semester following the semester the incomplete grade was given. The incomplete extension form must be obtained from the Office of the Registrar and requires the student’s signature and the faculty’s approval. The deadline to submit the extension to the Office of the Registrar is the last day to resolve an incomplete grade as posted on the Academic Calendar. [6]

**Registrar**: Phone: (201) 684-7695. Email: reg@ramapo.edu. Office: D-224. [22]

question: whats the max credits i can take in a semester and can i go over it
good_reply: 18 credits a semester. More needs a credit overload request through the Registrar (form), at extra cost; the GPA rule is 3.0 (the catalog says a student under 3.0 needs the advisor's approval first), and over 20 credits needs the school dean's approval.
must_not: Leaving out how to go over the limit. Invented people, numbers, rooms or dates.

body.answer:
Typically, you can take up to 18 credits per semester. [9]

Office of the Provost: For Fall and Spring A, a matriculated student who wishes to register for more than 18 credits per semester (at additional cost) must request that the Office of the Registrar raise their credit limit. [2] If the student has under a 3.0 cumulative GPA, they must obtain approval from their academic advisor before making the request. [2] If the student is attempting to register for more than 20 credits, they must obtain approval from their school Dean. [2]

Center for Student Success (Academic Advising): A student can request more than the allotted 18 credits by applying for a credit overload. [9] The student must have above a 3.0 GPA or be a graduating senior to be granted the overload. [9] The credit overload request form can be found here ([https://www.ramapo.edu/registrar/credit-overload-request-form/](https://www.ramapo.edu/registrar/credit-overload-request-form/)). [9]

Registrar: The credit overload request form is used when an undergraduate student wishes to take more than 18 credits or a graduate student wishes to take more than the maximum for their program. [12] A credit overload is ONLY granted if the student has a 3.0 GPA or above. [12] Credit overloads will incur additional charges. [12]

- **Center for Student Success (Academic Advising)**: Phone: (201) 684-7441. Email: success@ramapo.edu. Office: D-207. [25]
- **Office of the Provost**: Phone: (201) 684-7330. Email: provost@ramapo.edu. Location: first floor of the Birch Mansion. [25]

Sources: [2](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/pages/R532kjMfIcfnIkM0srb3#credit-load) [9](https://www.ramapo.edu/studentsuccess/policies/) [12](https://www.ramapo.edu/registrar/credit-overload-request-form/) [25](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/)

good_reply: Not this semester: the last day to request pass/fail or audit was Sep 3, 2026 for full-semester courses (Oct 20 for Session II). Audit gives no credit at the same tuition and fees, by form to the Registrar; the next chance is Spring 2027 (Jan 27, 2027 for full-semester courses).

question: i think my final grade is wrong, how do i appeal it and is there a deadline
good_reply: Within 20 calendar days after grades post, appeal in writing (email or certified letter) to the instructor with documentation; they have 15 days to decide. If no agreement, a written appeal to the dean of the school that sponsored the course within 20 days (15 days to decide), then a petition to the Office of the Provost within 20 days. Valid grounds: computational error, work not graded, a College policy violation (not wanting a higher GPA).
must_not: Stopping at the first step; no deadline. Invented people, numbers, rooms or dates.

body.answer:
That's stressful, but one bad grade doesn't decide everything. Talking with your professor and an advisor soon can really help.

Deadline: You must raise the appeal in writing with the course instructor no later than twenty calendar days after grades are posted. [3] The Office of the Provost says grade appeals are considered only when supported by documentation; possible grounds include a computational error, factual information not considered when the grade was posted, or an alleged College Policy violation. [2]
1. Email or send a certified letter to the course instructor, with supporting documentation. [3]
2. If you cannot agree and want to continue, send a written appeal by email or certified letter, including pertinent course materials or course work, to the Dean of the academic unit that sponsored the course within twenty calendar days of the final determination conference with the instructor. [3]
The Office of the Provost does not give the grade-posting date here, so I can’t determine your specific deadline. [3]

**Office of the Provost**: Phone: (201) 684-7330. Email: provost@ramapo.edu. Location: first floor of the Birch Mansion. [31]

This office can help:
**Center for Student Success (Academic Advising)**: Phone: (201) 684-7441. Email: success@ramapo.edu. Office: D-207. [32]

facts.says: Circumstances for which students may appeal gradesGrade appeals will be considered only if a student can provide documentation supporting their case.

Circumstances that might justify a grade appeal include (but are not limited to): computational error; factual information not in evidence at the time the grade was posted (for example, an assignment that the student can document was submitted but was not graded by the course instructor and therefore not factored into the final grade); or an alleged violation of College Policy.

If circumstances such as those described above can be documented, the student may appeal a grade by taking the following steps: No later than twenty calendar days after the posting of grades, a student must bring their appeal to the attention of the course instructor in writing by email or certified letter.
Supporting documentation must be provided.
Both parties should make good faith efforts to share viewpoints and mediate differences of opinion.
Students and instructors have up to 15 calendar days to reach a determination of grade.

If a student and the course instructor cannot reach an agreement and a student wishes to further pursue a grade appeal, the student must present a written appeal (by email or certified letter), including pertinent course materials or course work, to the Dean of the academic unit which sponsored the course in question within twenty calendar days of the final determination conference between the student and the course instructor.

The Dean will confer with the student and the course instructor, jointly or independently as they see fit, review pertinent documents and course materials, and confer with other faculty or administrative staff members as appropriate.
If the Dean determines that a grade change is not warranted, the course instructor and student will be so informed in writing by email.
The Deans have 15 calendar days to make this determination.

question: if i drop a class and go part time will i lose my financial aid
good_reply: Aid is adjusted below full time (12 credits): federal aid needs at least 6 credits; going from 12 to 6 reduces a Pell Grant but federal loans can be kept; state aid may be canceled; Ramapo grants and scholarships (merit scholarships need 12 credits) may be reduced or taken away. Talk to Financial Aid before dropping.
must_not: Leading with "I can't see your records" instead of the rules (a short note at the end is fine). Invented people, numbers, rooms or dates.

body.answer:
It depends. Financial Aid says dropping below full-time status will adjust your financial aid [1]. Federal aid requires 6 credits in a semester [1], and should not be affected if you remain enrolled for 6 or more credits [2]. If you go from full time status 12 credits to part time status 6 credits, your federal pell will be reduced but you can keep your federal loans [1]. NJ State aid (ie TAG, EOF, etc) requires full-time enrollment when the aid is fully disbursed to your account [2]. If you have state aid that is subject to being canceled, and institutional grants and scholarships could also be reduced or taken away [1]. If you drop below full-time status which is less than 12 credits, your Academic Scholarship or Ramapo grant may be taken away or reduced for the semester [3]. Contact the Office of Financial Aid to discuss your situation before making a change that drops you below full-time status for the semester [3].

**Financial Aid**: Phone: (201) 684-7549. Email: finaid@ramapo.edu. Office: E-210. [11]

Sources: [1](https://www.ramapo.edu/finaid/faqs/) [2](https://www.ramapo.edu/finaid/faqs/) [3](https://www.ramapo.edu/finaid/academic-merit-scholarships-terms-conditions/) [11](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/)

question: can i still add a class this semester

- Wednesday, October 21, 2026: Session II Courses - Last Day to Add/Drop for 100% Tuition Refund (already passed)
- Thursday, December 17, 2026: Last Day to Add/Drop Winter Classes with 100% Tuition Refund (also on the Winter 2027 calendar)

question: i have a medical condition, how can i request a housing accommodation
good_reply: Step 1: register with OSS (Application for Affiliation plus documentation from a licensed provider). Step 2: the Housing Accommodation Student Request Form and Provider Documentation Form. Step 3: meet Residence Life's deadlines. A committee (OSS, Residence Life, Health, Counseling) decides within 21 business days of complete documentation. OSS: 201-684-7514, oss@ramapo.edu, C-205.
must_not: Leaving out a step. Invented people, numbers, rooms or dates.

body.answer:
You can ask for support with that.

1. Office of Specialized Services (OSS): First register for affiliation. Submit comprehensive disability documentation from a licensed physician, psychiatrist, psychologist, social worker, or certified learning disabilities specialist so OSS can establish eligibility and determine appropriate accommodations or adjustments. [4]
2. Office of Specialized Services (OSS): See “How To Request OSS Services” ([https://www.ramapo.edu/oss/how-to-request-oss-services/](https://www.ramapo.edu/oss/how-to-request-oss-services/)) for more information. [4] If requesting only a strobe alarm, roll-in shower, wheelchair/mobility accessible residence hall, or 1st floor, you do not need the Housing Accommodation Student or Provider Request Forms; complete only a request for disability support form. [4]
3. Housing & Residence Life: Once affiliated, OSS informs the Office of Residence Life of residents needing specific housing accommodations based on medical documentation provided to OSS. [1][3]
4. Housing & Residence Life: Submit requests for Spring 2027 by December 15, 2026. That deadline is still to come. [3]

- **Office of Specialized Services**: Phone: (201) 684-7514. Email: oss@ramapo.edu. Location: C-Wing, Room 205. [11]
- **Housing & Residence Life**: Phone: (201) 684-7461. Email: reslife@ramapo.edu. [11]

Sources: [1](https://www.ramapo.edu/reslife/apply/) [3](https://www.ramapo.edu/reslife/new-student-guide/) [4](https://www.ramapo.edu/oss/housing-accommodations/) [11](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/)

citations.title: #1 - Register with the Office of Specialized Services

pageFacts.question: How can I request a housing accommodation for a medical condition?

facts.says: Any resident, who is requesting specific housing accommodations, due to a medically related condition, will need to register with the Office of Specialized Services (OSS).
Once affiliated, OSS will inform the Office of Residence Life of any residents who require specific housing accommodations based on medical documentation provided to their office.
Once affiliated, OSS will inform the Office of Residence Life of all residents who require specific housing accommodations based on medical documentation provided to their office.
Please submit requests for housing accommodations for the Spring 2027 semester by December 15, 2026.
All students requesting a housing accommodation based on a disability must first register for affiliation with the Office of Specialized Services (OSS).
Check out our webpage “How To Request OSS Services” (https://www.ramapo.edu/oss/how-to-request-oss-services/) for more information.

Comprehensive documentation of a disability from a licensed physician, psychiatrist, psychologist, social worker, or certified learning disabilities specialist must be submitted in order to establish eligibility and to determine which accommodations and/or adjustments are appropriate for each student.

Note: Students requesting only a strobe alarm, roll-in shower, wheelchair/mobility accessible residence hall, or 1st floor do not need to complete the Housing Accommodation Student or Provider Request Forms, as below.
Students only need to complete a request for disability support form.
Students can expect a decision about their request within twenty one (21) business days of OSS receiving all requested documentation.

question: i broke my wrist and cant write for a few weeks. can OSS help me with notes and exams
good_reply: Yes, OSS serves students with temporary disabilities such as a broken limb: submit the Application for Disability Support and current documentation, then an intake meeting with the OSS Director or Assistant Director authorizes accommodations. OSS: 201-684-7514, oss@ramapo.edu, C-205.
must_not: Saying OSS only helps permanent disabilities. Invented people, numbers, rooms or dates.

body.answer:
You can ask for support with that.

It depends. The Office of Specialized Services supports students with temporary disabilities, and appropriate services are discussed and authorized based on current functional limitations. [13] Potential accommodations include notetakers or scribes and extended testing time or alternative testing arrangements. [6] Schedule a meeting on Connect with your OSS Counselor and request a notetaker during your meeting to review your accommodations for the semester. [4] After meeting with your OSS Counselor and/or requesting accommodations, you can make exam reservations in OSSOnline. [5]

**Office of Specialized Services**: Phone: (201) 684-7514. Email: oss@ramapo.edu. Location: C-Wing, Room 205. [23]

Sources: [4](https://www.ramapo.edu/oss/notetaking/) [5](https://www.ramapo.edu/oss/ossonline-info-tutorials/) [6](https://www.ramapo.edu/oss/disabilities-and-teaching-strategies-accommodations/) [13](https://www.ramapo.edu/oss/oss-services-accommodations/) [23](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/)

question: i got a parking ticket. how do i pay or appeal it and how long do i have
good_reply: Appeal online within 20 days of the citation (appeal form; reviewed by the Parking Appeals Board). A citation not paid or appealed within 20 days gets a $5 late fee (another $5 after 28 days), and the right to appeal is lost after 20 days. Payment as the page says.
must_not: Leaving out the 20-day limit. Invented people, numbers, rooms or dates.

body.answer:
You have 20 days from citation issuance to pay or appeal before a $5 late fee may apply [1][3].

Public Safety:
1. Appeal online within twenty (20) days of issuance using the appeal form: [https://cm.maxient.com/reportingform.php?RamapoCollege&layout_id=3](https://cm.maxient.com/reportingform.php?RamapoCollege&layout_id=3) [1]. Missing the deadline forfeits the right to appeal [2][4]. Citations not paid or appealed within 20 days are subject to a $5 late fee [3], and a second $5 late fee may be assessed after 28 days [5].
2. Pay online at [https://rcnjpublicsafety.omnigo.one/CESIReportExec/OCP/Main.aspx](https://rcnjpublicsafety.omnigo.one/CESIReportExec/OCP/Main.aspx). Enter Citation # and Fine Amount, search for Citation, select your Citation, and follow the field required [6]. Select Payment Method; once processed, your citation will be emailed to you to say that it is paid [7].

- **Public Safety (Non-Emergency)**: Phone: (201) 684-7432. Email: publicsafety@ramapo.edu. Office: C-102. [23]
- **Public Safety (Emergency)**: Phone: (201) 684-6666. Email: publicsafety@ramapo.edu. Office: C-102. [23]

Sources: [1](https://www.ramapo.edu/publicsafety/vehicle-citation-information/) [2](https://www.ramapo.edu/publicsafety/parking-regulations/) [3](https://www.ramapo.edu/publicsafety/parking-regulations/) [4](https://www.ramapo.edu/publicsafety/vehicle-citation-information/) [5](https://www.ramapo.edu/publicsafety/how-to-apply-for-a-parking-permit/) [6](https://www.ramapo.edu/policies/policy/1167/) [7](https://www.ramapo.edu/policies/policy/1167/) [23](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/)

question: how do i pay my student account bill online
good_reply: Log in to RCNJ Experience (Web Self-Service), open the Student Account Info card, then Bill & Payment Suite and Make Payment; pay by electronic check (checking/savings) or credit/debit card via PayPath. Bills are eBills only; a monthly payment plan exists. Student Accounts: studentaccts@ramapo.edu, (201) 684-7495.
must_not: Anything about the Accounting program.

body.answer:
Student Accounts:
1. Log into RCNJ Experience (Web Self-Service) ([https://experience.elluciancloud.com/rconj/](https://experience.elluciancloud.com/rconj/)), locate the Student Account Info card, click Bill & Payment Suite, then click the Make Payment tab. Select the term, click Continue, choose Credit Card via PayPath from the Payment Method drop-down, and click Select. Verify or modify the payment amount, click Continue to PayPath, read the non-refundable PayPath service fee disclaimer on the Welcome to the PayPath Payment Service! Screen, then click Continue. [6]
2. Review your entries. If any data is incorrect, click Change Information; to cancel the transaction, click Cancel. Click Submit to submit your payment; submitting accepts the non-refundable service fee. Print the Payment Confirmation Page for your records. The College reserves the right to change costs, dates and procedures at its discretion. [6]

**Student Accounts**: Phone: (201) 684-7495. Email: studentaccts@ramapo.edu. Location: D-Wing, First Floor. [11]

Sources: [6](https://www.ramapo.edu/student-accounts/methods/) [11](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/)

body.answer:
Title IX is in D-104. [1] Title IX: Kat McGee, J.D. Director of Title IX and Institutional Compliance: kmcgee@ramapo.edu To file a complaint at the College about an incident of discrimination and/or sexual misconduct: titleix@ramapo.edu [1]

Title IX's page "Who is the College’s Director of Title IX/Title IX Coordinator?" says: "Kat McGee, J.D. Director of Title IX and Institutional Compliance Office: D 104 (201) 684-7220 kmcgee@ramapo.edu (mailto:kmcgee@ramapo.edu)" [2]

Title IX's page "What does the Director of Title IX/Title IX Coordinator do?" says: "The Director of Title IX is responsible for ensuring effective and timely responses to complaints of sexual violence, misconduct, discrimination or harassment by implementing Title IX related policies, coordinating appropriate training and resources, and identifying ways to prevent future discrimination. This includes management of grievances, investigations, and the disposition of complaints of sexual harassment, violence, rape, and discrimination under the Sexual Misconduct Policy ([https://www.ramapo.edu/titleix/sexual-misconduct-policy/](https://www.ramapo.edu/titleix/sexual-misconduct-policy/))." This includes management of grievances, investigations, and the disposition of complaints of sexual harassment, violence, rape, and discrimination under the Sexual Misconduct Policy (https://www.ramapo.edu/titleix/sexual-misconduct-policy/). The Director of Title IX is responsible for monitoring the overall implementation of Title IX for the College and coordinating compliance efforts. The Director helps to ensure that all students, staff, administrators, and faculty are trained and educated about Title IX. The Director of Title IX reports to the Office of the General Counsel & Institutional Compliance.

question: tell me about the MPP
good_reply: The Public Policy MPP (Master of Public Policy) in the School of Social Sciences and Social Work, from its catalog description. The Public Policy 4+1 may be added.
must_not: Saying there is no such program; describing another program.

body.answer:
The Public Policy MPP is the Master of Public Policy in the School of Social Sciences and Social Work. It focuses on how government laws and policies shape people’s lives, and prepares students in research methods, quantitative and qualitative methods, and skills for work with or for public institutions. [1]

Requirements: take all seven required courses—PUBL 600 THE POLITICS OF POLICYMAKING; PUBL 601 FEDERAL PUBLIC POLICY & GOVERNANCE; PUBL 602 STATE & LOCAL PUBLIC POLICY; PUBL 616 ECONOMETRICS AND ANALYSIS; PUBL 618 PUBLIC MANAGEMENT; PUBL 621 POLITICAL ECONOMY; and PUBL 705 PUBLIC POLICY INTERNSHIP. Select 3 (at least 3) electives from ACCT 502 GOVERNMENT AND NOT-FOR-PROFIT ACCOUNTING; ACCT 625 INTERNATIONAL ACCOUNTING; BADM 501 DATA ANALYTICS; BADM 503 BUSINESS LAW, ETHICS & REGULATORY PRONOUNCEMENTS; DATA 601 INTRODUCTION TO DATA SCIENCE; DATA 670 DATA VISUALIZATION; MATH 570 APPLIED STATISTICS; MATH 685 INTRODUCTION TO EXPERIMENTAL DESIGN; MBAD 610 BECOMING A 21ST CENTURY LEADER; MBAD 625 CRISIS & CHANGE MANAGEMENT; NURS 660 LEADERSHIP AND INNOVATION IN HEALTHCARE; NURS 670 HEALTHCARE ECONOMICS AND FINANCE; NURS 808 HEALTH POLICY LEADERSHIP; MSWK 505 SOCIAL WELFARE PROGRAMS AND POLICIES I; MSWK 507 CULTURAL DIVERSITY, RACISM, OPPRESSION AND PRIVILEGE; MSWK 604 ADVANCED SOCIAL POLICY; MSWK 610 PUBLIC HEALTH IN WEST AFRICA; or MSWK 670 SOCIAL WELFARE POLICIES IN HEALTH AND MENTAL HEALTH. [1]

Also published: Public Policy 4+1 and Public Policy Minor. [1] See the [MPP catalog page](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/programs/SO-MPP-PBPL). [1]

Graduate Admissions lists one professional or academic recommendation, a 400-word personal statement describing your interest, its fit with your intellectual development, and what you expect to accomplish, plus a resume. Enter references’ names and contact information in the online application’s “Recommendations” section; Ramapo sends them an automated request, and they upload directly to the application portal. The letter is waived for current Ramapo students graduating in 2027 and recent Ramapo graduates from 2025 and 2026. [6] See [Graduate Admissions requirements](https://www.ramapo.edu/graduate/requirements/). [6]

**Graduate Admissions**: Phone: (201) 684-7270. Email: graduate@ramapo.edu. Location: McBride House. [12]

Sources: [1](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/programs/SO-MPP-PBPL) [6](https://www.ramapo.edu/graduate/requirements/) [12](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/)

question: what's the RN to BSN
good_reply: The Nursing RN to BSN track, for registered nurses with an associate's degree or diploma who return for the BSN; one of three BSN tracks (generic, accelerated, RN to BSN); accredited by ACEN.
must_not: Invented people, numbers, rooms or dates.

body.answer:
Nursing RN to BSN is a Bachelor of Science in Nursing track designed for registered nurses prepared at the Associate’s degree or Diploma level to return for a BSN. Students transfer credits from their initial nursing program and complete Ramapo’s general education and nursing requirements. Ramapo’s nursing programs are accredited by the Accreditation Commission for Education in Nursing (ACEN). [1]

The BSN program also has generic and accelerated tracks. [1]

RN to BSN requirements: Required Math Course—select 1: MATH 108 ELEMENTARY PROBABILITY AND STATISTICS, PSYC 242 STATISTICS, or SOCI 308 DATA ANALYSIS IN SOCIOLOGY. RN to BSN Professional Core—required courses all of: NURS 312 NURSING INFORMATICS; NURS 316 PATHOPHYSIOLOGY; NURS 325 NURSING RESEARCH AND EVIDENCE BASED PRACTICE; NURS 330 HEALTH ASSESSMENT ACROSS THE LIFESPAN; NURS 425 COMMUNITY CENTERED NURSING; NURS 445 LEADERSHIP IN A GLOBAL WORLD; NURS 460 CLINICAL MANAGEMENT. Elective—select 1; students should consult their Nursing advisor for elective course options. [1]

Diploma nursing program graduates are granted 30 credits for their diploma nursing courses upon satisfactory completion of their first two BSN nursing courses. [1] Also published: Nursing Accelerated BSN, Nursing Generic BSN, and Nursing MSN. [1]

Sources: [1](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/programs/SN-BSN-NURS)

question: how many classes is the public health minor and which ones count
good_reply: Five courses: BIOL 204 Epidemiology, plus one each from statistics/research methods, health policy and management, social and behavioral science, and global or population health, with examples from each list.
must_not: Leaving out a course group. Invented people, numbers, rooms or dates.

body.answer:
The Public Health Minor consists of five courses (20 credits). [1] Take BIOL 204 EPIDEMIOLOGY, plus one course from each category: [1]
• Statistics or Research Methods: BADM 225, ENSC 345, MATH 370, NURS 325, PSYC 242, PSYC 303, SOCI 307, or SWRK 307. [1]
• Health Policy and Management: COMM 383, ECON 332, ENST 317, MGMT 330, NURS 445, or PUBL 201. [1]
• Social and Behavioral Science: SCIN 310, SOCI 230, SWRK 230, SWRK 328, PHLT 305, or PHLT 390. PHLT 305 is 4 credits, with no published prerequisites. [1][4]
• Global or Population Health: ANTH 307, NURS 220, NURS 365, NURS 425, PHLT 290, SOCI 309, or SPAN 311. NURS 365 and NURS 425 are marked as required courses in this category. [1]
BIOL 204 is 4 credits; prerequisite: BIOL 111 FUNDAMENTALS OF BIOLOGY I LECTURE. [1][3] NURS 365 is 4 credits, with no published prerequisites. [6] NURS 425 is 4 credits; it has the WRITING INTENSIVE (WRIT) attribute. Prerequisites (minimum grade: C+): CRWT 102 CRITICAL READING AND WRITING II or CRWT 102S CRITICAL READING AND WRITING II; NURS 340 FAMILY CENTERED NURSING; NURS 345 HEALTH ISSUES MANAGEMENT I; NURS 355 INTEGRATIVE CLINICAL STRATEGIES II; NURS 370 PATHOPHYSIOLOGY/PHARMACOLOGY I. Corequisites: be enrolled in NURS 410 HEALTH ISSUES MANAGEMENT II, NURS 430 INTEGRATIVE CLINICAL STRATEGIES III, and NURS 435 PATHOPHYSIOLOGY/PHARMACOLOGY II. [7]
PHLT 300 IS-PUBLIC HEALTH (4 credits; no published prerequisites) and ENST 355 ENVIRONMENTAL HEALTH are not listed in the minor requirements. ENST 355 is 4 credits and requires one of ENST 103, ENST 207, or GEOG 202. [1][2][5]

Sources: [1](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/programs/SN-MN-PHLT) [2](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/courses/PHLT300) [3](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/courses/BIOL204) [4](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/courses/PHLT305) [5](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/courses/ENST355) [6](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/courses/NURS365) [7](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/courses/NURS425)

question: what happens if i take an incomplete and don't finish the work in time? can i get more time
good_reply: An I needs the instructor's approval and at least two-thirds of the course done. Work not finished by the date on the academic calendar turns the I into an F. In extraordinary circumstances a student can request an extension, up to the end of the following semester, on the Registrar's form with the student's signature and the faculty member's approval, due by the last day to resolve incompletes (Feb 12, 2027 for fall incompletes).
must_not: Leaving out that it becomes an F, or that an extension exists. Invented people, numbers, rooms or dates.

body.answer:
The Fall 2026 academic calendar lists [21]:
- Friday, October 16, 2026: Session I Courses - Last Day to Request an Incomplete ("I" Grade) (already passed)
- Tuesday, December 15, 2026: Full and Session II Courses - Last Day to Request an Incomplete ("I" Grade)

Yes, in extraordinary circumstances you may request an incomplete extension. [6]

The Registrar says that if you do not satisfactorily complete the work by the completion date on the Incomplete Form or academic calendar—whichever is earlier—your grade changes to F. If completed by then, the assigned grade replaces the I. Review Academic Calendar ([https://www.ramapo.edu/academic-calendars/](https://www.ramapo.edu/academic-calendars/)) for Incomplete Deadlines; the Incomplete Form must be completed by you and your instructor. [4]

The extension can last only until the end of the semester following the semester the I was given. Obtain the incomplete extension form from the Office of the Registrar; it needs your signature and faculty approval. Submit it by the last day to resolve an incomplete grade posted on the Academic Calendar. [6] Submit the form to reg@ramapo.edu. [4]

**Registrar**: Phone: (201) 684-7695. Email: reg@ramapo.edu. Office: D-224. [22]

Sources: [4](https://www.ramapo.edu/registrar/grading-options/) [6](https://www.ramapo.edu/registrar/grading-options/) [21](https://www.ramapo.edu/academic-calendars/) [22](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/)

pageFacts.question: what happens if i take an incomplete and don't finish the work in time? can i get more time

facts.says: If the work is completed by the completion date indicated on the Incomplete Form or the academic calendar (the earliest date will be honored), the grade assigned replaces the I. If the work is not satisfactorily completed by the completion date the grade is changed to F. Requesting an Incomplete Grade: Review the Academic Calendar (https://www.ramapo.edu/academic-calendars/) for Incomplete Deadlines The Incomplete Form must be completed by the student and the instructor.
The form must be submitted to the Office of the Registrar: reg@ramapo.edu (mailto:reg@ramapo.edu).
In extraordinary circumstances a student may request an incomplete extension.

question: whats the max credits i can take in a semester and can i go over it
good_reply: 18 credits a semester. More needs a credit overload request through the Registrar (form), at extra cost; the GPA rule is 3.0 (the catalog says a student under 3.0 needs the advisor's approval first), and over 20 credits needs the school dean's approval.
must_not: Leaving out how to go over the limit. Invented people, numbers, rooms or dates.

body.answer:
18 credits per semester is the typical limit. [9]

Office of the Provost: For Fall and Spring, a matriculated student who wishes to register for more than 18 credits per semester (at additional cost) must request that the Office of the Registrar raise their credit limit. [2] If the student has under a 3.0 cumulative GPA, that student must obtain approval to raise the credit limit from their academic advisor prior to making the request to the Office of the Registrar. [2] If the student is attempting to register for more than 20 credits, they must obtain approval from their school Dean. [2]

Center for Student Success (Academic Advising): A student can request to take more than the allotted 18 credits by applying for a credit overload. [9] The student must have above a 3.0 GPA or be a graduating senior to be granted the credit overload. [9]

Registrar: The credit overload request form is used when an undergraduate student wishes to take more than 18 credits or a graduate student that wishes to take more than the maximum for their program. [12] A credit overload is ONLY granted if the student has a 3.0 GPA or above. [12]

question: i think my final grade is wrong, how do i appeal it and is there a deadline
good_reply: Within 20 calendar days after grades post, appeal in writing (email or certified letter) to the instructor with documentation; they have 15 days to decide. If no agreement, a written appeal to the dean of the school that sponsored the course within 20 days (15 days to decide), then a petition to the Office of the Provost within 20 days. Valid grounds: computational error, work not graded, a College policy violation (not wanting a higher GPA).
must_not: Stopping at the first step; no deadline. Invented people, numbers, rooms or dates.

body.answer:
That's stressful, but one bad grade doesn't decide everything. Talking with your professor and an advisor soon can really help.

Office of the Provost: Your first deadline is no later than twenty calendar days after grades are posted. [3]
1. Put your appeal to the course instructor in writing by email or certified letter, and provide supporting documentation. [3]
2. If you cannot reach an agreement and want to continue, send a written appeal with pertinent course materials or coursework to the Dean of the academic unit that sponsored the course within twenty calendar days of the final determination conference with the instructor. [7]
3. If the Dean’s opinion does not support your appeal, you may petition the Office of the Provost for a review. [10]

pageFacts.question: i think my final grade is wrong, how do i appeal it and is there a deadline

facts.says: Circumstances for which students may appeal gradesGrade appeals will be considered only if a student can provide documentation supporting their case.

Circumstances that might justify a grade appeal include (but are not limited to): computational error; factual information not in evidence at the time the grade was posted (for example, an assignment that the student can document was submitted but was not graded by the course instructor and therefore not factored into the final grade); or an alleged violation of College Policy.

If circumstances such as those described above can be documented, the student may appeal a grade by taking the following steps: No later than twenty calendar days after the posting of grades, a student must bring their appeal to the attention of the course instructor in writing by email or certified letter.
Supporting documentation must be provided.
Both parties should make good faith efforts to share viewpoints and mediate differences of opinion.
Students and instructors have up to 15 calendar days to reach a determination of grade.

If a student and the course instructor cannot reach an agreement and a student wishes to further pursue a grade appeal, the student must present a written appeal (by email or certified letter), including pertinent course materials or course work, to the Dean of the academic unit which sponsored the course in question within twenty calendar days of the final determination conference between the student and the course instructor.

The Dean will confer with the student and the course instructor, jointly or independently as they see fit, review pertinent documents and course materials, and confer with other faculty or administrative staff members as appropriate.
The Deans have 15 calendar days to make this determination.
If the Dean renders an opinion which does not support the student’s grade appeal, the student may petition for a review by the Office of the Provost.

question: if i drop a class and go part time will i lose my financial aid
good_reply: Aid is adjusted below full time (12 credits): federal aid needs at least 6 credits; going from 12 to 6 reduces a Pell Grant but federal loans can be kept; state aid may be canceled; Ramapo grants and scholarships (merit scholarships need 12 credits) may be reduced or taken away. Talk to Financial Aid before dropping.
must_not: Leading with "I can't see your records" instead of the rules (a short note at the end is fine). Invented people, numbers, rooms or dates.

body.answer:
It depends. Financial Aid says dropping below full-time status will adjust your financial aid [1]. Federal aid should not be affected if you remain enrolled for 6 or more credits [2]; at 6 credits, federal Pell is reduced but you can keep federal loans [1]. NJ State aid requires full-time enrollment when the aid is fully disbursed to your account [2]. Your Academic Scholarship or Ramapo grant may be reduced or taken away for the semester if you drop below 12 credits [3]. Contact the Office of Financial Aid before making a change that drops you below full-time status [3].

**Financial Aid**: Phone: (201) 684-7549. Email: finaid@ramapo.edu. Office: E-210. [11]

Sources: [1](https://www.ramapo.edu/finaid/faqs/) [2](https://www.ramapo.edu/finaid/faqs/) [3](https://www.ramapo.edu/finaid/academic-merit-scholarships-terms-conditions/) [11](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/)

If you drop below full-time status which is less than 12 credits your Academic Scholarship or Ramapo grant may be taken away or reduced for the semester.
Please contact the Office of Financial Aid to discuss your situation before making a change that drops you below full-time status for the semester.

good_reply: Step 1: register with OSS (Application for Affiliation plus documentation from a licensed provider). Step 2: the Housing Accommodation Student Request Form and Provider Documentation Form. Step 3: meet Residence Life's deadlines. A committee (OSS, Residence Life, Health, Counseling) decides within 21 business days of complete documentation. OSS: 201-684-7514, oss@ramapo.edu, C-205.
must_not: Leaving out a step. Invented people, numbers, rooms or dates.

body.answer:
You can ask for support with that.

1. Register for affiliation with the Office of Specialized Services (OSS). [4]
2. Submit comprehensive documentation of a disability from a licensed physician, psychiatrist, psychologist, social worker, or certified learning disabilities specialist so OSS can establish eligibility and determine appropriate accommodations. [4]
3. Check out the webpage “How To Request OSS Services” ([https://www.ramapo.edu/oss/how-to-request-oss-services/](https://www.ramapo.edu/oss/how-to-request-oss-services/)) for more information. [4]
4. If requesting only a strobe alarm, roll-in shower, wheelchair/mobility accessible residence hall, or 1st floor, you do not need to complete the Housing Accommodation Student or Provider Request Forms; complete a request for disability support form instead. [4]
5. Once affiliated, OSS will inform the Office of Residence Life of residents who require specific housing accommodations based on medical documentation provided to their office. [1]
6. Submit requests for housing accommodations for the Spring 2027 semester by December 15, 2026. [3]

- **Office of Specialized Services**: Phone: (201) 684-7514. Email: oss@ramapo.edu. Location: C-Wing, Room 205. [11]
- **Housing & Residence Life**: Phone: (201) 684-7461. Email: reslife@ramapo.edu. [11]

Sources: [1](https://www.ramapo.edu/reslife/apply/) [3](https://www.ramapo.edu/reslife/new-student-guide/) [4](https://www.ramapo.edu/oss/housing-accommodations/) [11](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/)

question: i broke my wrist and cant write for a few weeks. can OSS help me with notes and exams
good_reply: Yes, OSS serves students with temporary disabilities such as a broken limb: submit the Application for Disability Support and current documentation, then an intake meeting with the OSS Director or Assistant Director authorizes accommodations. OSS: 201-684-7514, oss@ramapo.edu, C-205.
must_not: Saying OSS only helps permanent disabilities. Invented people, numbers, rooms or dates.

body.answer:
I'm sorry you're dealing with that, and I hope you feel better soon.

1. Office of Specialized Services provides information and support to Ramapo College students with permanent and temporary disabilities. [13]
2. A wrist injury may affect writing, and OSS lists notetakers and scribes as potential accommodations. [14]
3. Schedule a meeting on Connect with your OSS Counselor and request a notetaker to review your accommodations for the semester. [4]
4. Log into OSSOnline to review your courses and select your accommodations; your counselor is notified to review and approve them. [7]
5. For on campus exams, submit an exam reservation through OSSOnline no later than 7 days before the scheduled exam or 14 days before an on campus final exam. [8]

**Office of Specialized Services**: Phone: (201) 684-7514. Email: oss@ramapo.edu. Location: C-Wing, Room 205. [23]

This office can help:

question: can i have an emotional support animal in my dorm, and how does approval work
good_reply: Call OSS at 201-684-7514 and meet with the OSS Director; documentation from a health care or mental health professional is needed; the animal may come only after OSS approval (Residence Life pets rule); it may be limited to defined areas, generally not academic or recreational buildings.
must_not: Invented people, numbers, rooms or dates.

body.answer:
It depends: you may have an Emotional Support Animal on campus only after registering with the Office of Specialized Services (OSS), providing documentation showing the benefits of the animal, and receiving an accommodation permitting it [3]. The Office of Specialized Services reviews requests and, in most cases, the Housing Accommodation Request Committee does too [8]. OSS and/or the committee decide whether the request is reasonable and may deny it if it is unreasonable or insufficiently documented [5][4]. For an animal request, the College may ask its age and size/breed, if applicable [6]. Please call the Office of Specialized Services at 201-684-7514 to discuss your interest [1].

**Office of Specialized Services**: Phone: (201) 684-7514. Email: oss@ramapo.edu. Location: C-Wing, Room 205. [27]

Sources: [1](https://www.ramapo.edu/oss/housing-accommodations/) [3](https://www.ramapo.edu/oss/campus-accessibility-and-services-information/service-support-animal-policy/) [4](https://www.ramapo.edu/oss/housing-accommodations/) [5](https://www.ramapo.edu/oss/frequently-asked-questions/) [6](https://www.ramapo.edu/policies/policy/centers-institutes-guidelines/) [8](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/pages/R532kjMfIcfnIkM0srb3#academic-policy-approval-process) [27](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/)

Please plan accordingly.

question: i got a parking ticket. how do i pay or appeal it and how long do i have
good_reply: Appeal online within 20 days of the citation (appeal form; reviewed by the Parking Appeals Board). A citation not paid or appealed within 20 days gets a $5 late fee (another $5 after 28 days), and the right to appeal is lost after 20 days. Payment as the page says.
must_not: Leaving out the 20-day limit. Invented people, numbers, rooms or dates.

body.answer:
You have 20 days from the citation’s issuance to appeal. [1]

Public Safety: Submit an appeal online through the [Appeal Portal](https://cm.maxient.com/reportingform.php?RamapoCollege&layout_id=3); the owner/driver must appeal within twenty (20) days of issuance. [1] Missing the deadline forfeits the right to appeal. [1][3] Citations not paid or appealed within 20 days are subject to a $5 late fee. [3] A second $5 late fee may be assessed after 28 days. [3]

To pay online through the [Payment Portal](https://rcnjpublicsafety.omnigo.one/CESIReportExec/OCP/Main.aspx): [4]
1. Enter Citation # and Fine Amount. [4]
2. Search for Citation, select your Citation and follow the field required. [4]
3. Select Payment Method. Once processed, your citation will be emailed to you to say that it is paid. [4]

- **Public Safety (Non-Emergency)**: Phone: (201) 684-7432. Email: publicsafety@ramapo.edu. Office: C-102. [23]
- **Public Safety (Emergency)**: Phone: (201) 684-6666. Email: publicsafety@ramapo.edu. Office: C-102. [23]

Sources: [1](https://www.ramapo.edu/publicsafety/vehicle-citation-information/) [3](https://www.ramapo.edu/publicsafety/parking-regulations/) [4](https://www.ramapo.edu/publicsafety/vehicle-citation-information/) [23](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/)

Failure to file the appeal within twenty (20) days constitutes forfeiture of the right to appeal.

You must FIRST stop at the Parking and ID Office, Rm. C101, or contact parking services at parking@ramapo.edu (mailto:parking@ramapo.edu), to ensure that the fine has been transferred to your student account.

question: how do i pay my student account bill online
good_reply: Log in to RCNJ Experience (Web Self-Service), open the Student Account Info card, then Bill & Payment Suite and Make Payment; pay by electronic check (checking/savings) or credit/debit card via PayPath. Bills are eBills only; a monthly payment plan exists. Student Accounts: studentaccts@ramapo.edu, (201) 684-7495.
must_not: Anything about the Accounting program.

body.answer:
Student Accounts:
1. Log into RCNJ Experience (Web Self-Service) ([https://experience.elluciancloud.com/rconj/](https://experience.elluciancloud.com/rconj/)), locate the Student Account Info card, click Bill & Payment Suite, then click the Make Payment tab at the top of the page. [6]
2. Select the term you wish to make payment for and click Continue. From the Payment Method drop down, select Credit Card via PayPath and click Select. Verify or modify the payment amount, then click Continue to PayPath. Read the non-refundable PayPath service fee disclaimer on the Welcome to the PayPath Payment Service! Screen, then click Continue. [6]
3. Review your entries. If any data is incorrect, click Change Information; if you do not wish to have your transaction processed, click Cancel. Click Submit to submit your payment. By submitting your entry, you are accepting to pay the non-refundable service fee. Print the Payment Confirmation Page for your records. [6]

**Student Accounts**: Phone: (201) 684-7495. Email: studentaccts@ramapo.edu. Location: D-Wing, First Floor. [11]

Sources: [6](https://www.ramapo.edu/student-accounts/methods/) [11](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/)
